items.title: Indonesia strengthens measures against stock manipulation after market rout triggered by MSCI
items.author: Stefanno Sulaiman
items.creator: Stefanno Sulaiman
items.summary: Indonesia on Monday introduced more measures to address stock market manipulation, including adding independent parties to a committee determining stocks with concentrated ownership structures, after MSCI said the country could be demoted due to concerns about opaque trading.
items.body:
Indonesia on Monday introduced more measures to address stock market manipulation, including adding independent parties to a committee determining stocks with concentrated ownership structures, after MSCI said the country could be demoted due to concerns about opaque trading.
The measures came after MSCI announced earlier this month that it could demote Indonesia's stock exchange to [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:""standalone" market status"], saying not enough had been done to [USN:L4N46509U TEXT:"arrest coordinated trading practices"] in its stock market.
That was more severe than the global index provider's January warning that it could downgrade the country to "frontier" status. At present, MSCI still classifies Indonesia as an "emerging" market.
The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) plans to expand the membership of a committee that comes up with a list of stocks with high shareholder concentration to include independent parties like Indonesian academics and F. Chapman Taylor as a representative of foreign investors, chief Jeffrey Hendrik said at a press conference.
Previously, the committee members were officials from capital market authorities. Taylor is a former partner with investment company the Capital Group and is currently an adviser to Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund, Danantara.
"We encourage the IDX to strengthen the mechanism and methodology of trading supervision, including its capacity to identify patterns of irregular transactions, detect coordinated trading and strengthen the mechanism to respond to such events," said Hasan Fawzi, the financial regulator's capital market supervisor.
Last week, the IDX said it would [USN:L1N46804O TEXT:"exclude stocks"] with high shareholding concentrations from its main Jakarta index (.JKSE) starting on November 2. The current list includes 80 companies.
The MSCI downgrade warning spurred Indonesia's deepest-ever two-day stock selloff on October 16 and 19, sending the main index to its lowest point since 2020. It has since rebounded.
At 0320 GMT on Monday, the index was down around 0.6%. The rupiah weakened 0.4% to its weakest point since July.
POSSIBLE COORDINATED TRADING TRIGGERS INVESTIGATION The exchange also plans to launch investigations when it detects possible coordinated trading to manipulate share prices and freeze suspicious investor accounts, Hendrik said.
The new measure, to take effect in November, is more proactive than the IDX's previous response. The IDX previously warned public investors of unusual market activities when a stock price moved sharply and requested an explanation from the company. The process could also lead to a temporary freeze in share trading.
A policy that allows share buybacks without requiring approval from a general shareholders meeting has also been extended until June 2027, Hasan said, adding that any buyback must consider rules about the minimum free float, or shares available to trade in the market.
Hasan said Indonesia has been communicating with MSCI and other global index providers like FTSE Russell to reiterate its regulators' commitment to market reforms.
The market showed resilience following MSCI's (MSCI.N) recent announcement, Hasan said, describing local investors as "mature" and "wise" for buying stocks in companies with good fundamentals.
President Prabowo Subianto told his cabinet last week that MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but said the country would not be afraid, striking a combative tone in his first public reaction to the [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"downgrade "][USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"warning"].
Since MSCI's January warning, Indonesia has launched a series of reforms including releasing more details on investor accounts and ownership data, increasing the minimum free-float level and unveiling [USN:L1N4670MN TEXT:"record fines"] against parties involved in market manipulation.

items.title: India's Shriram Finance hits 11-month low as growth outlook cut, credit costs weigh
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Shares of India's Shriram Finance fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender lowered its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit.
items.body:
Shares of India's Shriram Finance (SHMF.NS) fell to an 11-month low on Monday after the non-bank lender [USN:L4N4690PL TEXT:"lowered"] its annual loan growth forecast and warned of higher credit costs, overshadowing a better-than-expected second-quarter profit.
Shares fell as much as 6.13% to 810.20 rupees, extending losses from Friday, and were on track for an eighth consecutive session of declines.
The company cut its assets under management growth forecast for fiscal 2027 to 15%-17% from 18%, citing weak monsoon conditions and geopolitical uncertainty, and flagged pressure on borrowers in drought-hit regions.
Jefferies said credit costs could remain elevated for another one to two quarters as stress rises in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,145 rupees from 1,210 rupees.
Higher slippages and write-offs reflected drought-like conditions in several states, Motilal Oswal said, adding that the lender's overall asset quality remained broadly stable.
JM Financial said rising early-stage delinquencies and drought-related stress among rural borrowers remained key concerns for Shriram Finance. The brokerage maintained its "buy" rating but cut its target price to 1,025 rupees from 1,175 rupees, citing deteriorating asset quality indicators.
Shriram Finance reported a nearly 60% jump in second-quarter profit to 36.77 billion rupees ($387.30 million) on Friday, beating analysts' estimate of 35.46 billion rupees, according to LSEG-compiled data.
($1 = 94.9400 Indian rupees)

items.title: Investors expect Brazilian stocks, currency to fall after Lula reelected
items.author: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres
items.creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres
items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won reelection on Sunday, defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and setting up a test for financial markets, with investors expecting recent bets on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead.
items.body:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"won reelection on Sunday"], defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and setting up a test for financial markets, with investors expecting recent bets on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead.
November futures for the Brazilian real were down 10% in Asian hours while a Tokyo-listed Brazilian stock exchange-traded fund, the Nomura NF Ibovespa Link ETF (1325.T) , plunged 15%.
Markets had moved sharply in anticipation of a right-wing shift since Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro, unexpectedly finished first in the opening round three weeks ago.
Stocks (.BVSP) closed on Friday almost 7% above their level going into the first round, while the real currency was nearly 5% stronger against the US dollar. Interest-rate futures had indicated expectations that tighter public finances would allow borrowing costs to decline.
"We expect a sharp market reaction on Monday, with aggressive repricing, a selloff in assets and interest rate futures likely to hit their upper limit shortly after the open," said Luis Felipe Vital, head of macro strategy at Warren Investimentos.
Over the next four years, Lula must slow the growth of Brazil’s debt while protecting social programs and investment. For investors, the question is whether his gradual approach to fixing public finances can bring borrowing costs down.
Without confidence that he can deliver, lenders could demand higher interest rates, adding to the government’s debt and making credit more expensive for businesses and households.
"Investors want a clear and credible commitment to fiscal discipline," said Alejo Czerwonko, chief investment officer for emerging markets at UBS Global Wealth Management. "We expect the rally that followed the first round to be largely priced out, and sentiment to stay weak until a clear fiscal plan emerges."
Czerwonko said investors are looking for a halt to the spending that accompanied the campaign and a believable path to stabilize public debt. "It also means a working relationship with an opposition-leaning Congress, because no fiscal plan passes without it," he said.
Lula’s team aims to produce a budget surplus before interest payments of about 1.3% of gross domestic product by 2030. That would leave money to cover part of the interest bill, reducing the need for fresh borrowing. But public debt already exceeds 82% of GDP, while pensions and other legally required spending limit where savings can come from.
"Lula's policies have talked about spending cuts, but he's not gone into the details of how that is going to look like," said Divya Singaravelu, head of research at Meridian 1305 Capital. She said the choice of the next finance minister would be an early signal to markets, adding: "We want to see what the 2027 budget and spending cap looks like."
Whoever takes the job will need to explain how campaign commitments fit within those fiscal limits.
"The key point is that, even if pessimism prevails in the near term, investors will need to watch how the government's economic agenda advances over the medium term," said Gustavo Sung, chief economist at Suno Research.
"The main thing to watch now is how the government organizes itself for 2027."

items.title: How purchases of sanctioned Iranian jet fuel were disguised by Myanmar
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: In December 2025, the US-sanctioned tanker Reef arrived in Myanmar waters with some 113,000 barrels of fuel backed by sham paperwork.
items.body:
In December 2025, the US-sanctioned tanker Reef arrived in Myanmar waters with some 113,000 barrels of fuel backed by sham paperwork.
Myanmar-based energy broker Dynamic Wave ordered the shipment, agreeing in a sales contract inked with Thailand’s Tawan-Oil Trading to supposedly take delivery of a similar amount of South African diesel. But the $15.8 million agreement, which Reuters viewed, was a charade: there was no such trade between South Africa and Myanmar in 2025, according to data from the United Nations and Vortexa, a shipping and energy data provider.
In reality, Reef carried jet fuel from Iran to Myanmar, according to records of fuel shipments to Myanmar, as well as satellite images and analysis by SynMax Intelligence, which tracked the tanker’s journey from the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas to Southeast Asia.
The deception was needed because the US in 2023 imposed targeted sanctions on Myanmar’s jet-fuel industry. The US [USN:L1N35V1MA TEXT:"did so citing the deadly bombing campaign"] waged by the Southeast Asian country’s military on civilian targets as part of an effort to crush a rebel-led insurgency. All purchasers of Iranian oil and fuel are also exposed to sweeping American sanctions.
Details of how Myanmar disguised purchases of Iranian jet fuel, as well as the entities involved in the transactions, are reported here for the first time.
Myanmar’s military junta was involved in the ruse. Days before Reef arrived, Myanmar’s foreign exchange regulator told the client of Dynamic Wave that it would issue import documentation that labeled the delivery as diesel “instead of jet fuel,” according to a copy of the agency’s November 30 letter seen by Reuters. The document, which was provided to Reuters by the activist group Justice for Myanmar, did not explain the purpose of the mislabeling.
The letter from the regulator also authorized Dynamic Wave and its client, National Energy Prime Aviation Services Company, to pay Tawan for the shipment.
Neither Dynamic Wave nor its client, which is part-owned by Myanmar’s military-backed government, responded to questions about the fuel shipment.
Spokespeople for Myanmar’s military-backed government and foreign exchange regulator, as well as the Iranian foreign ministry, also did not return requests for comment.
Tehran was the Myanmar military’s primary supplier of jet fuel between October 2024 and December 2025, with much of the trade carried out by the tankers Reef — since renamed Maris — and Noble, a Reuters report revealed in January.
The scheme uncovered by Reuters underscores both the reach and limits of Washington’s power. The lengths taken to disguise the trade suggest US sanctions are biting. But Iranian jet fuel has continued to flow, earning Tehran valuable foreign currency and providing Myanmar with the means to conduct both commercial aviation and air raids.
The US Treasury did not respond to questions about jet-fuel shipments between Iran and Myanmar.
JET FUEL, AIRSTRIKES AND CIVILIAN CASUALTIES Myanmar’s generals seized power in 2021 from the democratically elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup sparked a civil war, during which the military has killed thousands — including many civilians — in aerial assaults, the United Nations said in August.
Myanmar’s foreign ministry said in response to the UN allegations that the military “exercises maximum restraint to avoid civilian harm.”
Justice for Myanmar, which also shared the fuel sales contract with Reuters, published a report on Monday concluding that Myanmar’s junta was importing jet fuel mislabeled as diesel.
The organization, which supports further sanctions on Myanmar's jet fuel imports, said it obtained the documents from a junta-run server that was briefly publicly accessible.
Reuters found a dead link to one of the documents on the DuckDuckGo search engine, indicating it had once been hosted on that server. Delivery dates and fuel quantities in the documents also match Iranian jet fuel shipment records that were separately reviewed by the news agency.
THAI BANK CONNECTION The sales contract for Dynamic Wave's fuel shipment stipulated that the payment be transferred into Tawan’s account at Siam Commercial Bank (SCB), Thailand’s oldest bank.
Tawan was identified by UN experts in a 2024 report as a jet-fuel supplier to Myanmar’s military. The firm has not commented on those allegations.
SCB was described as a major facilitator of Myanmar military procurement in that report.
The bank said after the report’s release that it adheres to anti-money-laundering laws and that its Myanmar-related transactions were legitimate and not connected to the arms trade.
Reuters could not determine whether SCB was aware of the nature of Tawan’s business.
Thai regulators in 2024 ordered banks to closely scrutinize transactions involving Myanmar in order to comply with sanctions and anti-money-laundering laws.
SCB did not respond to repeated requests for comment about its commercial relationship with Tawan.
Tawan and the Bank of Thailand, which supervises the kingdom's financial industry, also did not respond to questions.
The December shipment was not the first time jet fuel arrived in Myanmar disguised as diesel.
Dynamic Wave in May 2025 agreed to buy from Tawan 202,000 barrels of what a second contract, also obtained from the junta server, described as South African diesel. The agreement stipulated that the diesel should arrive at Yangon within a month and that Dynamic Wave would pay $26 million into Tawan’s SCB account.
The invoice for that contract contained discrepancies suggesting the tanker actually contained jet fuel.
The density of the fuel listed in the document matched the specifications for jet fuel rather than diesel sold in Southeast Asia, according to Joshua Heyne, a jet-fuel expert at Washington State University, and data from Platts, the energy-industry information provider. In addition, the price of the fuel was more than 50% higher than a global diesel benchmark.
Noble called at Yangon on June 17 carrying just under 200,000 barrels of jet fuel earmarked for Dynamic Wave, shipment records show.
Like Reef's December shipment, Noble’s cargo was loaded at Iran’s Bandar Abbas according to SynMax’s analysis of satellite imagery. As it made its way to Myanmar’s commercial capital, Noble transmitted location signals that made it appear as though its destination was the port of Chittagong in Bangladesh, according to SynMax.
The manager of the Reef and Noble tankers did not respond to questions sent via its listed website.
Shipments of jet fuel between Iran and Myanmar have continued this year, Reuters [USN:L6N45U0Y7 TEXT:"reported in October"], citing SynMax analysis and satellite imagery.

items.title: France protest loss estimates: As demonstrations enter third week, how much could retailers lose as shops remain shut
items.author: Swati Gandhi
items.summary: French retailers face mounting losses as protests bring looting, damage and store closures. Carrefour has warned of a hit of up to €200 million to annual operating profit, while luxury brands have boarded up shops and increased security amid fears of further unrest.
items.body: Peaceful student protests that began in France in September over teacher shortages, inadequate education funding, and deteriorating school conditions have widened to include public anger over the government’s handling of the high cost of living and have turned violent. As demonstrations continue, with clashes and looting in some cities, the impact is starting to show.From popular tourist attractions such as the Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais being shut to retailers closing stores amid fears of further looting and damage, the unrest is disrupting tourism and trade. Hotel bookings in Paris have taken a hit, while retailers across the country are estimating massive losses from damaged and ransacked stores.How much could French retailers lose as protests continue?According to Euronews, at least 3,000 French shops were hit during the 17–18 October protests. While insurers said they were mobilised, lost trade may not be covered, depending on whether businesses have business interruption insurance.Insurers did not reveal the number of claims filed after stores were ransacked or provide an initial estimate of losses during the 17–18 October protests. For comparison, the 2023 riots, which swept the country in June and July, resulted in €793 million in insured losses, according to France Assureurs. Insurers processed approximately 17,000 claims, with an average payout of about €46,600. Shops and commercial properties accounted for two-thirds of the total, or roughly €523 million. Nearly €200 million, a quarter of the total, covered losses suffered by local authorities following attacks on town halls, schools and buses. Vehicles accounted for the remaining seven per cent.On 19 October, French supermarket giant Carrefour’s chief executive, Alexandre Bompard, who also chairs the FCD retail federation, estimated that roughly 1,500 shops were affected. He put the industry’s losses at several hundred million euros. The supermarket giant alone reported damage to at least 50 of its stores, including 20 that were looted.On 21 October, shares in Carrefour, which is also France’s largest listed retail group, declined by over 13% after the company warned that violent protests across the country could hurt its earnings, AFP reported. The retailer estimated that the unrest would reduce its operating profit for the year by €80 million–€200 million ($90 million–$225 million).How did French businesses prepare for fresh weekend protests?According to Reuters, luxury retailers across France covered their shop windows with boards and brought in private security guards ahead of demonstrations on 24 October. Some also planned to remain shut following widespread looting during the previous weekend’s unrest.Staff at a Rolex retailer and a De Beers outlet near Place Vendôme in Paris said the stores would stay shut on 24 October. Other retailers, including Richemont-owned IWC, planned to assess the size of the demonstrations before deciding whether to close early.On the Champs-Élysées, Adidas and Boss displayed closure notices on windows reinforced with boards. Employees at Swatch Group outlets said they would shorten their trading hours.Metal cages surrounded a Lacoste store that had sustained “enormous” damage the previous week, according to a staff member. The brand’s café was also fully boarded up.Separately, staff at LVMH brands Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari told Reuters they were not taking any chances and had ramped up security at their stores near Place Vendôme. The group also deployed additional private security to patrol high-end shopping districts.With further demonstrations planned, retailers face continued uncertainty over store closures, security costs and lost sales(with inputs from agencies)

items.title: Raiders to consider starting No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak will consider whether No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza can be part of the solution as losses mount for Las Vegas since starting the season 3-0.
items.body:
Raiders coach Klint Kubiak will consider whether No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza can be part of the solution as losses mount for Las Vegas since starting the season 3-0.
The Raiders were plagued by familiar issues as they lost a fourth consecutive game Sunday, 35-21 to the Los Angeles Rams.
"I think at this point, we're thinking about everything," Kubiak said. "How to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter. Personnel, scheme, we've got to talk about all of it."
Kirk Cousins completed 26 of 44 passes for 295 yards and two touchdowns Sunday and his performance wasn't entirely detrimental to the Raiders. Las Vegas was 3-of-14 on third down and scored a touchdown on one of five trips to the red zone.
"It's really the same every day that it was in March or April," Cousins said when asked about ceding the position to Mendoza. "Nothing changes in the sense that, if I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there either. The first OTA, if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, ‘Yeah, you can't play me.'
"So nothing changes. The organization will do what they feel is best. I feel that Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead, and I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can, help us win, and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually."
Mendoza has completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards, all in mop up duty at New England on Oct. 11.
Cousins leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes and is 12th in the league with a 97.4 passer rating.
Drafted first overall in April, Mendoza was the Heisman Trophy winner and led Indiana to the national championship in 2025. But he's been QB2 most of his stint in Las Vegas.
Kubiak and general manager John Spytek made it clear Cousins, 38, would begin the 2026 season as the Raiders' starter.
Not executing in the red zone was the main issue that left Kubiak miffed on Sunday.
"It comes down to we have to make plays down there when we have our one-on-one opportunities," Kubiak said. "Got to make the throws, got to make the catches. Didn't happen."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Gap apparel supplier Gokaldas eyes doubling Europe exports share to cut US reliance
items.author: Praveen Paramasivam
items.creator: Praveen Paramasivam
items.summary: Indian apparel supplier Gokaldas Exports expects Europe to nearly double its share of exports as it benefits from a proposed trade deal, while diversifying beyond the US, a top executive told Reuters.
items.body:
Indian apparel supplier Gokaldas Exports (GOKL.NS) expects Europe to nearly double its share of exports as it benefits from a proposed trade deal, while diversifying beyond the US, a top executive told Reuters.
Domestic garment exporters are looking beyond the United States as uncertainty over tariffs persists, while anticipating stronger demand from Europe as India secures better trade access.
"Europe accounts for around 15% of our exports. Over the next three to five years, we expect Europe's share to increase to approximately 25%-30%," said Sivaramakrishnan Ganapathi, Gokaldas' vice-chairman and managing director.
The European Union is expected to sign [USN:L8N42P0VF TEXT:"a landmark trade deal"] with India by the end of 2026, cutting tariffs on imports.
Gokaldas is "actively holding discussions with major European retailers in preparation for duty-free trade," Ganapathi said without naming them, adding it is boosting capacity in India instead of moving production elsewhere.
The exporter, whose top customers include brands such as Gap, Carhartt, and JCPenney, is investing 1.25 billion rupees ($13.2 million) in fiscal 2027 to expand overall capacity and upgrade facilities.
Gokaldas, which counts Pearl Global Industries (PGIL.NS) and KPR Mill (KPRM.NS) among its peers, expects the US share of exports to moderate from 69%, seeking to cut exposure to tariff shocks and policy uncertainty. It did not say by how much the share would fall.
"The India–EU trade agreement could provide a medium-term opportunity to improve competitiveness, subject to implementation, product coverage and origin requirements," said Equirus Securities analyst Ronak Shah.
US apparel imports from across the globe fell 7% to $49.08 billion in January-August, government data showed.
But Gokaldas' US spring and summer orders for 2027 were stronger than the 2026 holiday season, when its shipments from India rose 3%-4% from a year earlier, Ganapathi said. He added that holiday sales would provide an early indication of demand for next year.
($1 = 94.9400 Indian rupees)

items.title: Grizzlies stay unblemished with victory at winless Kings
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Isaiah Stewart and Ty Jerome converted three-point plays to bookend a late 11-0 flurry and the Memphis Grizzlies remained undefeated with a 123-112 road victory over the winless Sacramento Kings on Sunday night.
items.body:
Isaiah Stewart and Ty Jerome converted three-point plays to bookend a late 11-0 flurry and the Memphis Grizzlies remained undefeated with a 123-112 road victory over the winless Sacramento Kings on Sunday night.
Jerome finished with 31 points while Cameron Boozer (16 points, 11 rebounds) and Cedric Coward (15 points, 11 rebounds) each recorded a double-double for the Grizzlies, who elected to rest star center Zach Edey on the first night of a road back-to-back set.
Memphis (3-0) plays at Utah on Monday night.
After blowing a 14-point lead and finding themselves in a 106-all tie with 5:41 remaining, the Grizzlies seized control again by scoring the game's next 11 points.
Stewart got the spurt rolling by turning a 5-footer into three points with a foul shot.
Coward made it a five-point game when he tipped in a Boozer miss on Memphis' next possession. Jerome then scored six straight points, three on a 27-footer and three on an 8-footer on which he was fouled and sank the resulting free throw.
Down 117-106 with 3:57 to play, the Kings got no closer than seven the rest of the way.
Jerome, who made all 14 of his free-throw attempts, also found time for a team-high six assists. Jaylen Wells chipped in with 16 points, while Stewart and Cam Spencer added 13 apiece.
Sacramento's Zach LaVine was the game's leading scorer with 37 points. Rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. had 22 to go with a game-high seven assists, while center Domantas Sabonis, fighting foul trouble much of the night, put up a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double.
Precious Achiuwa (12 points, 10 rebounds) also had a double-double for the Kings, who have lost all three of their games on the young season.
Seeking to open 3-0 for the first time since 2017, the Grizzlies used an 11-0 run early in the second quarter to take a lead that eventually grew to double digits before halftime and 83-69 in the fifth minute of the third quarter.
But the Kings eventually drew even at 106-all on a three-point play by Sabonis with 5:41 remaining, setting the stage for the Grizzlies' late surge.
--Field Level Media

items.title: サウジ、シンガポールで原油貯蔵へ　アジアの供給安定強化
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Florence Tan　Jeslyn Lerh

[シンガポール ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Florence Tan　Jeslyn Lerh

[シンガポール ２６日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアとシンガポールのエネルギー相は２６日、サウジが２０２７年後半からシンガポールの地下石油貯蔵施設「ジュロン・ロック・キャバーンズ」に原油を貯蔵する計画だと明らかにした。地域の安定供給を強化する狙い。

米国とイスラエルによるイランとの戦争により、ホルムズ海峡を経由するアジア向け石油供給には大きな混乱が生じた。戦争前、アジアは原油輸入量の３分の２を中東に依存していた。

シンガポールのタン・シーレン・エネルギー・貿易・産業相は、国際会議「シンガポール国際エネルギー週間」で「サウジとシンガポールは２７年後半からジュロン・ロック・キャバーンズにサウジ産原油を貯蔵する枠組みを構築するという共同の意向を表明する」と述べた。

「この枠組みは東南アジアにおけるサウジ産原油の供給網の強靱性を高めるとともに、供給が途絶した際のシンガポールのエネルギー安全保障と対応力の向上に寄与する」とした。

同氏によると、サウジ国有石油会社サウジアラムコは２６日にシンガポールのエネルギー市場監督庁（ＥＭＡ）、ＪＴＣコーポレーションと覚書を締結し、数カ月以内の交渉妥結を目指す。

サウジのアブドルアジズ・エネルギー相は録画メッセージで「供給拠点をアジアの主要市場に近づけることで、われわれの供給網の柔軟性が高まり、シンガポールの供給の安定性と備えを支えることになる」と述べた。

ジュロン島の地下１５０メートルにある同施設は、原油やコンデンセートなどの液体炭化水素を最大１４７万立方メートル貯蔵できる。

アラムコは現在、日本と韓国で原油を貯蔵しており、予期せぬ供給不足が生じた際には現地政府が優先的に購入できる。

items.title: India's Infosys falls after revenue growth view cut flags AI, competitive pressures
items.author: Mridula Kumar, Sai B
items.creator: Mridula Kumar, Sai B
items.summary: Shares of India's Infosys fell 2.7% on Monday after the software exporter sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast, underscoring challenges from AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets.
items.body:
Shares of India's Infosys (INFY.NS) fell 2.7% on Monday after the software exporter sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast, underscoring challenges from AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets.
The firm was the last of the top 5 to report [USN:L6N45T0UF TEXT:"earnings"] for the Indian IT sector. Earlier this month, peers Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) and HCLTech (HCLT.NS) met revenue estimates with modest margin performance, but investors cheered the uptick in AI revenue.
The company cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth [USN:L6N4680ZX TEXT:"forecast"] to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, while most analysts had expected it to trim only the upper end of the range to 2.5%.
"Peers are better placed than Infosys at this point, and the share movement is just reflecting that. Infosys has been underperforming from Q4FY26 results," LKP Securities analyst Anshul Jethi said.
AI competition and clients expanding their global capability centres or offshore tech hubs directly, rather than engaging Infosys for IT services, are also hurting the company, he added.
Systematix analysts called it a "disappointing quarter", highlighting pricing pressure from heightened competition and client productivity demands on account of AI, and subdued tech spending among retail and high-tech clients.
Brokerage Motilal Oswal said weaker volumes, smaller-than-expected price increases, a shift toward offshore delivery and Infosys' decision to exit a large European manufacturing contract had weighed on growth.
TD Cowen said macroeconomic uncertainty, AI-led productivity demands, and heightened competition have hurt pricing and volumes, while seasonal weakness and client ramp-downs could weigh on second-half growth.
Analysts rate the stock "Buy" on average, with a median price target of 1,180 rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Shares were last trading 1.5% lower at 1,136 rupees as of 10:53 a.m. IST. The Nifty IT (.NIFTYIT) index was down 0.2% while the benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) index was up 0.16%.

Oct 26 : Shares of India's Infosys fell 2.7 per cent on Monday after the software exporter sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast, underscoring challenges from AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets.
The firm was the last of the top 5 to report earnings for the Indian IT sector. Earlier this month, peers Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech met revenue estimates with modest margin performance, but investors cheered the uptick in AI revenue.
The company cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1 per cent-2 per cent from 1.5 per cent-3 per cent, while most analysts had expected it to trim only the upper end of the range to 2.5 per cent.
"Peers are better placed than Infosys at this point, and the share movement is just reflecting that. Infosys has been underperforming from Q4FY26 results," LKP Securities analyst Anshul Jethi said.

AI competition and clients expanding their global capability centres or offshore tech hubs directly, rather than engaging Infosys for IT services, are also hurting the company, he added.
Systematix analysts called it a "disappointing quarter", highlighting pricing pressure from heightened competition and client productivity demands on account of AI, and subdued tech spending among retail and high-tech clients.
Brokerage Motilal Oswal said weaker volumes, smaller-than-expected price increases, a shift toward offshore delivery and Infosys' decision to exit a large European manufacturing contract had weighed on growth.
TD Cowen said macroeconomic uncertainty, AI-led productivity demands, and heightened competition have hurt pricing and volumes, while seasonal weakness and client ramp-downs could weigh on second-half growth.
Analysts rate the stock "Buy" on average, with a median price target of 1,180 rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Shares were last trading 1.5 per cent lower at 1,136 rupees as of 10:53 a.m. IST. The Nifty IT index was down 0.2 per cent while the benchmark Nifty 50 index was up 0.16 per cent.

items.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil pumping stations, Riyadh airport as fighting intensifies
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport, as rising hostilities choke oil supplies and threaten to erupt into a larger conflict.
items.body:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport, as rising hostilities choke oil supplies and threaten to erupt into a larger conflict.
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said earlier it had destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in the capital Sanaa, including one used to fire a missile towards Riyadh that the coalition said it had intercepted.
There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi attacks.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war.
The Houthis also said they had struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"resumed operations at two terminals"] on Sunday after an attack claimed by the group [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"earlier this month"] killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
Top officials from the Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are set to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional coordination, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
The planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia came under escalating attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.
STRIKES INSIDE YEMEN Saudi Arabia [USN:L6N453173 TEXT:"temporarily shut down"] its 1,200-km (746-mile) East-West pipeline in September as a precaution after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said originated in Iraq. The pipeline has served as a key route for Middle East oil exports while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by the war.
The Houthis also said on Saturday they had targeted the East-West pipeline, crude oil pumping stations, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and the Rabigh refinery. There was no Saudi confirmation of those claims.
The Saudi coalition said on Monday it had also carried out a military operation against Houthi targets in Yemen, destroying five tunnels used to store ballistic missiles, four ballistic missile launchers and a missile storage facility.
The operation also targeted Houthi supply lines, fighters and military equipment along front lines inside Yemen, coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said, pledging continued "deterrent operational measures" to protect civilians.
Saudi Arabia has intensified its strikes on the Houthis since the group captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key global shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.
The latest fighting has effectively ended a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia led a coalition into Yemen's civil war in 2015 to back the internationally recognised government, a year after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

items.title: ＳＫハイニックス、28日に株主還元策発表へ　特別配当報道受け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ソウル ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ソウル ２６日 ロイター] - 韓国半導体大手ＳＫハイニックスは、四半期決算を公表する２８日に株主還元策を発表すると明らかにした。約１６兆ウォン（１２０億ドル）の特別配当を検討しているとの報道を受けた。

韓国紙の東亜日報は２６日、ＳＫハイニックスが日本の半導体メモリーメーカー、キオクシアホールディングスの株式売却益を原資に特別配当を検討していると報じた。

ＳＫハイニックスは今年完了した株式売却の詳細を公表していないが、アナリストは、累計で多額の投資利益を計上したと推定している。

同社は２０１８年、米投資会社ベインキャピタルが主導する日米韓の投資家連合を通じ、キオクシアに約４兆ウォンを投資した。

ＳＫハイニックスは報道について証券取引所から問われた際、「さまざまな株主還元策を検討している」とし、２８日に第３・四半期決算と合わせて発表する予定だと説明した。詳細には踏み込まなかった。

米エヌビディアに製品を供給するＳＫハイニックスとサムスン電子は、人工知能（ＡＩ）向けメモリー半導体の需要急増を背景に過去最高益を計上し、配当や自社株買いを通じて余剰資金をより多く還元するよう投資家からの圧力が強まっている。

ＳＫハイニックスは８月、４０兆ウォン相当の自社株買いおよび消却を実施し、２５─２７年に生み出されるフリーキャッシュフローの５０％超を株主還元の拡充に充てると発表した。

また同社は２３日、市場の変動を理由に、半導体子会社ソリダイムの米国上場計画を一時停止したと発表した。この計画には投資家や規制当局から懸念が示され、同社株の重荷となっていた。

items.title: The week in Asian football
items.author: Michael Church
items.creator: Michael Church
items.summary: Talking points from the week in Asian football:
items.body:
Talking points from the week in Asian football:
SEOUL CROWNED CHAMPIONS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2016 FC Seoul's 1-1 draw with Gangwon FC on Saturday secured the club a first league title in a decade as nearest rivals Ulsan HD were held 2-2 by Pohang Steelers.
Moon Seon-min put hosts Seoul ahead in the 58th minute before Kang Joon-hyuck levelled six minutes.
Seoul, who claimed their seventh league title, are 16 points clear of Ulsan with five matches left.
CHINESE TITLE RACE GOES TO THE WIRE AS CHENGDU LOSE The Chinese Super League title race will go down to the final week of the campaign after leaders Chengdu Rongcheng lost 1-0 to second-placed Dalian Yingbo on Saturday.
Chengdu have needed a point from their previous three matches to claim their first title but have lost them all. They will get another chance to claim the point they need when they face Shandong Taishan on November 8.
Chengdu's Felipe Silva missed a penalty before Mamadou Traore scored the winner for Dalian, who face Tianjin Tiger in their final game.
AL-HILAL RETURN TO TOP SPOT IN SAUDI PRO LEAGUE Al-Hilal won 3-2 against Al-Qadsiah on Friday to replace Brendan Rodgers' side at the top of the Saudi Pro League, while champions Al-Nassr moved up to second.
Second-half goals from Ruben Neves and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic secured the win that took Al-Hilal two points clear of Al-Qadsiah, who have played one game more.
Al-Nassr defeated hosts Al-Faisaly 3-1 to move ahead of Al-Qadsiah on goal difference.
MACHIDA STAY TOP DESPITE DRAW WITH VISSEL KOBE FC Machida Zelvia were held 0-0 by Vissel Kobe in Japan on Saturday but stayed top on goal difference ahead of FC Tokyo, who thrashed Mito Hollyhock 6-0.
Machida and Tokyo are on 27 points, one point ahead of Sanfrecce Hiroshima, who won 4-0 against Shimizu S-Pulse.
WELLINGTON PHOENIX CONTINUE PERFECT START Wellington Phoenix beat Central Coast Mariners 2-0 on Sunday to pick up their second straight victory to start the new A-League season, with two goals in two second-half minutes from Rafael Duran and Corban Piper.
Defending champions Auckland FC lost 5-2 to Western Sydney Wanderers.

items.title: China's yuan climbs to fresh 4-year high ahead of key policy meetings
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: China's yuan climbed to a fresh four-year high against the dollar on Monday, extending its longest winning streak since May, as softer oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, ahead of key policy meetings at home and overseas.
items.body:
China's yuan climbed to a fresh four-year high against the dollar on Monday, extending its longest winning streak since May, as softer [USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"oil prices"] and US Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, ahead of key policy meetings at home and overseas.
Investors were cautious ahead of major central bank meetings due later this week, with the US Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan and European Central Bank widely expected to keep rates unchanged while maintaining a hawkish tone. Attention will also turn to China's [USN:L6N46C04K TEXT:"fifth plenum"] for fresh policy clues.
Prior to market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate at 6.7162 per dollar, its strongest since February 2, 2023. The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day.
Monday's midpoint was 471 pips weaker than a Reuters estimate of 6.6691 — its largest weak-side deviation since September 23.
The central bank has been gradually strengthening its daily yuan official guidance this year, but at levels weaker than market expectations, suggesting it is seeking to manage the pace of appreciation, traders and analysts said.
"The PBOC continues to resist a faster pace of appreciation via weaker than-market-expected fixings," analysts at Barclays said in a note.
"We think the PBOC's reaction function points to a stronger floor against disorderly weakness, while the fixing should continue to constrain the pace of gains as the trade-weighted currency strengthens."
In the spot market, the onshore yuan hit a high of 6.6682 per dollar at one point, the strongest level since June 2022, before last trading at 6.6691 as of 0252 GMT.
If it retains the gains at the late-night close, the onshore spot yuan would have booked an eighth straight session of rises, the longest winning streak since May.
Its offshore counterpart last fetched 6.6688 per dollar, up about 0.01% in Asian trade.
"We continue to think that a gradual but sustained currency appreciation is underway but consensus forecasts and forward markets underestimate how far this process can run given the deep undervaluation starting point," Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note.
"Ultimately, currency appreciation alone will not address China's economic challenges ... that needs both currency appreciation and support for domestic demand, two instruments to hit two targets," they said, maintaining their 12-month target for the yuan at 6.40 per dollar.

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: アップル初の折り畳みスマートフォン「iPhone
items.body: アップル初の折り畳みスマートフォン「iPhone Duo（デュオ）」が10月23日に発売され、オンライン予約では瞬く間に初回在庫が完売した。サムスンなどの先行機が存在する中、ヒンジの耐久性や画面技術など多くの課題を抱える初代機となっている。望遠レンズがないなどカメラ機能で妥協した点や、外部の開発者によるアプリが新しい画面サイズに対応し切れていない点は、一部の購入者を失望させる可能性があると指摘されている。著名なレビュアーの中には、多くのアップルユーザーにはDuoを勧めない人もいるという。

items.title: Pachuca gana de visita a líder América en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pachuca regresó a la senda del triunfo tras vencer el domingo 2-1 de visita al líder América en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
items.body:
Pachuca regresó a la senda del triunfo tras vencer el domingo 2-1 de visita al líder América en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
Los "Tuzos" de Pachuca, que no ganaban desde el 11 de septiembre en la octava jornada, vencieron a las "Águilas" con goles de Alan Bautista y del neerlandés Oussama Idrissi.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de la Ciudad de México, Pachuca se adelantó a los 12 minutos por conducto de Bautista, quien definió con un disparo raso desde fuera del área.
América empató en el inicio de la segunda parte cuando Henry Martín remató con el pecho en el área chica un centro de Erick Sánchez en una jugada donde los elementos del equipo local hilaron varios pases a los 46 minutos.
Pachuca logró la victoria a los 74 minutos con un potente disparo de Idrissi desde fuera del área.
En los minutos restantes, América presionó en busca del empate que estuvo cerca de conseguir, pero las atinadas intervenciones del portero Carlos Moreno lo evitaron.
A pesar de la derrota, América se mantiene como líder del torneo con 27 puntos, mientras que Pachuca se ubicó en la decimotercera posición con 16 unidades.
“Venimos aquí con la cara en alto, con el pecho erguido, contra el súper líder en su casa y, a mi parecer, jugamos mejor partido. Pero no quiere decir que echemos las campanas al vuelo y nos relajemos, al contrario, es la catapulta más importante para cerrar dignamente el torneo, no nos queda más que salir a luchar, competir y jugar lo mejor que podamos", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Pachuca, Benjamín Mora.
"Tenemos que ser muy consistentes para sumar la mayor cantidad de puntos que podamos", agregó.
En los otros partidos disputados el domingo, el actual campeón Cruz Azul venció 3-1 de visita a Querétaro con goles de Andrés Montaño, del argentino Nicolás Ibáñez y del nigeriano Christian Ebere. Para los "Gallos Blancos" de Querétaro anotó el argentino Mateo Coronel.
Atlas venció 4-3 a Puebla con tantos de los argentinos Florián Monzón y Kevin Zenón, y doblete de José Martín. Para Puebla anotaron el venezolano Luifer Hernández, el defensa Paulo Ramírez en su propia portería y Omar Moreno.
Por su parte, Tijuana goleó 4-1 a Santos Laguna con tantos del argentino Francisco González, del uruguayo José Ignacio Rivero en dos ocasiones y del ecuatoriano Adonis Preciado. Para los "Guerreros" de Santos anotó Esteban Lozano.
El sábado, Guadalajara ganó 1-0 de visita a Monterrey, Pumas UNAM y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1, mismo marcador que se registró en el partido entre León y Toluca.
El viernes, Atlético de San Luis ganó de visita al Atlante por 1-0. Por su parte, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1.

items.title: Seahawks knock Chiefs from unbeaten ranks in decisive fashion
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as the host Seattle Seahawks defeated Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.
items.body:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as the host Seattle Seahawks defeated Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.
Wilson had 24 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown run around the left end with 3:47 remaining to clinch the victory for the defending Super Bowl champions.
NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III, who was the MVP of the Seahawks' 29-13 Super Bowl victory against New England before signing with Kansas City as a free agent in the offseason, was limited to 36 yards on 14 carries on Sunday night.
Patrick Mahomes was 19-of-33 passing for 165 yards with an interception for the Chiefs (5-1), who had just 213 yards of total offense to the Seahawks' 410. Tight end Travis Kelce had four receptions for 44 yards.
Sam Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards with one touchdown and one interception for the Seahawks (4-3).
Darnold hit Smith-Njigba on a 28-yard scoring strike down the left sideline with 1:44 left in the first half, giving the Seahawks a 10-0 lead. Smith-Njigba was originally ruled out of bounds inside the 1-yard line, but a video review determined the ball had crossed the goal line. The drive started after safety Ty Okada intercepted a Mahomes pass.
The Chiefs went three-and-out on the ensuing possession, giving the ball back to Seattle with 1:16 remaining.
The Seahawks reached the Kansas City 2 before Chiefs cornerback Nohl Williams intercepted a pass in the back of the end zone and returned it to Seattle's 44.
Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker was short on a 58-yard attempt on the final play of the half, leaving the score at 10-0.
Jason Myers kicked a pair of field goals for the Seahawks, including a 25-yarder with 8:22 remaining in the second quarter to open the scoring.
The Seahawks took the second-half kickoff and Myers made a 35-yarder to increase the lead to 13-0.
The Chiefs' lone score came on Butker's 50-yard field goal with 1:42 left in the third quarter.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack, state media says
items.author: Yomna Ehab
items.creator: Yomna Ehab
items.summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported.
items.body:
Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported.
Friday's attack during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, also wounded 40 others. [USN:L6N46B02Q TEXT:"Witnesses "]said the shooting lasted several minutes.
Jordan's Public Security Directorate said the suspects were located while hiding in an abandoned house in Karak. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding them, the directorate said in a statement published on state media.
No security personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession.
Jordanian authorities have said the violence was carried out by "extremist terrorists". There has been no claim of responsibility.
"Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate".
King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, has ordered security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on the Christian minority.
Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist militant plots over the years.
The Public Security Directorate did not name the suspects or publicly identify possible affiliations with any Islamist militant groups.
Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young people towards extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.

items.title: Bank of Japan's hawkish pause to leave scope for December hike
items.author: Leika Kihara
items.creator: Leika Kihara
items.summary: The Bank of Japan will likely declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2% inflation target at its policy meeting on Friday and emphasise the risks prices could overshoot, signaling the chance of a rate hike as soon as December.
items.body:
The Bank of Japan will likely declare victory in a nearly 14-year battle to hit its 2% inflation target at its policy meeting on Friday and emphasise the risks prices could overshoot, signaling the chance of a rate hike as soon as December.
Such hawkish language may reinforce expectations the [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"BOJ"], [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"US Federal Reserve"] and [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"European Central Bank"] will all raise rates by year-end, as brisk AI demand and the Iran war-induced energy shock worsen global inflationary pressures.
Still, the BOJ is likely to avoid dropping explicit hints on the timing and pace of future rate rises as it balances the need to forestall risks of an inflation overshoot without disrupting jittery markets with a premature hike, analysts say.
"With rises in prices and wages moderate, the BOJ will keep raising rates gradually without rushing," said a person familiar with its thinking, a view echoed by two more people.
At the two-day policy meeting ending on Friday, the BOJ is set to maintain its policy rate at 1.25% by a majority vote, forgoing a back-to-back hike to spend more time scrutinising the effect of past rate hikes on lending conditions.
In a quarterly report due after the meeting, the BOJ is likely to slightly revise up next fiscal year's price forecast and signal that underlying inflation has roughly achieved its 2% target, [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"people familiar with the matter have told Reuters"].
With wage gains becoming embedded and inflation expectations hovering around 2%, the central bank will likely stress that it will now focus on anchoring inflation around its target by raising rates toward levels deemed neutral to the economy.
While Governor Kazuo Ueda has already signaled such a shift in policy focus upon raising rates in September, the pivot would mark another symbolic departure from the BOJ's prolonged efforts to fire up inflation through ultra-loose monetary policy.
"It's a historical moment for the BOJ, though it faces a more challenging task now that it needs to step not just on the accelerator but the brakes," said Naomi Muguruma, chief bond strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities.
"The BOJ will probably scrutinise upcoming data and market moves in deciding whether to raise rates in December, or hold until January," she said.
Analysts [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] expect the BOJ to raise rates to 1.5% in December and stick to a quarterly pace of rate hikes.
FUNDING STILL LOOSE Under former governor Haruhiko Kuroda, the BOJ deployed a massive stimulus in 2013 to pull Japan out of deflation and fire up inflation to its 2% inflation target.
Even after ending its mix of unorthodox easing steps in 2024, the central bank has trodden cautiously in raising rates on the view underlying inflation - or price moves excluding one-off factors and driven by domestic demand - remained below target.
With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised rates in September after delivering a hike in June - a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes in 2024 and 2025.
The BOJ's policy rate, at 1.25%, is now within the range of 1.1% to 2.5% its staff estimated as Japan's neutral rate, or the level that neither cools nor overheats the economy - drawing market attention to how far it could eventually hike rates.
With growth in bank lending still strong, the central bank is likely to stress on Friday that financial conditions remain loose - signalling scope for further rate hikes before its policy rate reaches levels close to neutral, the people said.
The BOJ's meeting follows that of the Fed, which is seen skipping a hike at its two-day meeting concluding on Wednesday. The ECB is also set to keep rates unchanged at 2.5% on Thursday.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE-ＳＨＥＩＮ、米ＦＴＣと1億ドルで和解へ　顧客の苦情巡る調査で
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Helen Reid　Jody Godoy

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Helen Reid　Jody Godoy

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - 中国発のファストファッションネット通販大手ＳＨＥＩＮ（シーイン）は、配送の遅延など顧客の苦情に関する米連邦取引委員会（ＦＴＣ）の調査について、１億ドルを支払って和解することに同意した。関係筋が２３日、ロイターに明らかにした。

和解金は同社の第２・四半期利益の４４％に相当。欧米で規制や税制面の締め付けに直面し、成長に急ブレーキがかかる同社にとって新たな打撃となる。

シーインはロイターに対する声明で「ＦＴＣと建設的な結論に達した」と述べ、近く追加情報を公表すると表明した。ＦＴＣの報道官はコメントを控えた。

同社は７月、香港上場に向けた提出書類で、米国の調査により多額の罰金を科される可能性があると警告していた。

ロイターが確認したＦＴＣの記録によると、２０２０年１月から２６年６月にかけて、総額１１００万ドル超の購入に関し、消費者から１万２０００件余りの苦情が寄せられていた。

苦情の一部は、配達済みと表示された荷物が顧客に届かず、シーインのカスタマーサービスも問題を解決しなかったなど、配送に関する内容だった。

ロイターは苦情の内容や、それらが最終的に解決されたかを独自に検証することはできなかった。

シーインは欧州連合（ＥＵ）で少額小包に３ユーロの手数料を課されたことなどで業績が打撃を受け、株価は９月１日の香港上場以来２２％下落している。ＥＵは１１月１日から２ユーロの追加取扱手数料を課す予定だ。

items.title: オーストリア、スパイ活動でロシア人外交官4人を国外追放に
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Francois Murphy

[ウィーン ２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Francois Murphy

[ウィーン ２３日 ロイター] - オーストリア外務省は２３日、「外交官としての身分にそぐわない活動」をしたことを理由として、ウィーン駐在のロシア人外交官４人を国外追放すると発表した。この表現は通常、スパイ（諜報）活動を実施した人物に対して用いられる。

今回の措置により、２０２０年以降にオーストリアが追放したロシア人外交官は計１８人となった。

外務省は声明で「オーストリアの治安当局による調査結果に基づき、オーストリア外務省はウィーン駐在のロシア人外交官４人に対して措置を講じた」とし、４人を「ペルソナ・ノン・グラータ（好ましからざる人物）」だと宣言。４人に国外退去を命じたことを明らかにした。

うち３人は駐オーストリアロシア大使館に、１人は欧州安保協力機構（ＯＳＣＥ）の軍事安全保障・軍備管理担当ロシア代表部に勤務していた。

オーストリアは中立国だが、２２年のロシアによるウクライナ侵攻後は政治的にウクライナ側に立っている。

これに対し、駐オーストリアロシア大使館はウェブサイト上の声明で「オーストリアは西側諸国の反ロシア政策を無思慮に受け入れており、こうした措置に対しては必然的に相応の対応を取ることになるだろう」と反発。４人の国外追放措置について、オーストリア当局によるロシアに対する「さらなる非友好的な措置」だと称した。

ウィーンにはＯＳＣＥのほか、国際原子力機関（ＩＡＥＡ）などの国連機関があり、外交上の主要な拠点の一つとなっている。

items.title: Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday
items.author: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid
items.creator: Andrew Mills, Ariba Shahid
items.summary: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in the wider Iran conflict.
items.body:
Top officials from Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in the wider Iran conflict.
Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkey by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said.
The talks come as attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Both countries have also drawn up plans to restart the wider war, possibly after the US midterm elections on November 3.
Monday's planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under [USN:L6N4440I6 TEXT:"the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
Qatari mediators met Iranian officials in Tehran on Sunday in a push to de-escalate regional tensions, Reuters reported. Qatar has, for months, played a key mediating role between Tehran and Washington.
A senior Iranian official said the meeting was initiated by Pakistan, during Munir's visit to Tehran [USN:S8N455017 TEXT:"last week"], as he met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials. During the visit, Iranian officials told him there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, according to Iranian media.
Earlier mediation efforts involving both Pakistan and Qatar helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the deal quickly unravelled as fighting between Iran and the United States resumed weeks later.
The deputy secretary of Iran's top security body, Ali Baqeri-Kani, told state TV that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid, Pakistan's Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin would visit Tehran for consultations with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on regional security.
Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the meeting is part of ongoing efforts by the Mecca Pact countries to de-escalate the current crisis, promote diplomatic solutions, and support mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan."The visit also underscores the pivotal role of the Mecca Pact states in fostering regional security and stability, and their commitment to working with all nations in the region toward achieving this goal," Krimly posted on X.
Pakistan's military media wing and Turkey's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
TENSIONS RISING Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the Houthis continued unabated.
Ministers from the Mecca Pact countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh earlier this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
The Houthi attacks have become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war.
Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran and Iran's leaders have said that a renewed US military campaign would be met with a stronger response than before.
Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again. A US intelligence memo this week warned that Iranian plots against American personnel had reached "advanced stages".
The war, now nearly eight months old, has weighed on President Donald Trump's approval ratings ahead of the midterms.
The Mecca agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters.
Efforts by Turkey’s parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last week.

items.title: Rupee weakens on importers' dollar payments, modest buildup in long dollar positions
items.author: Nimesh Vora
items.creator: Nimesh Vora
items.summary: The Indian rupee came under pressure after opening largely unchanged on Monday, with dollar purchases by importers and a modest buildup in long dollar interbank positions adding to the drag from high oil prices.
items.body:
The Indian rupee came under pressure after opening largely unchanged on Monday, with dollar purchases by importers and a modest buildup in long dollar interbank positions adding to the drag from high oil prices.
The rupee weakened through the morning, slipping 0.18% to 95.1150 per dollar by 11:10 a.m. IST.
The absence of central bank dollar sales, which had helped support the rupee in recent sessions, added to the currency's woes on Monday.
The weakness highlights the unit's struggle to withstand persistent external headwinds without regular support from the Reserve Bank of India.
Brent crude rose more than 6% last week to a six-month high amid concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on Saudi Arabia. Prices remained near $115 a barrel in Asia trading.
High oil prices widen India's import bill, add to inflationary pressures and weigh on economic growth. They can encourage companies to increase currency hedges and make foreign investors more cautious about Indian assets.
The rupee had found support in recent weeks from the Reserve Bank of India's interventions, which helped it recover from levels near 96.70 per dollar, and from Jio Platforms IPO-linked inflows.
In the absence of this support, the currency remains more exposed to dollar demand.
Another factor could come into play this week, with the Federal Reserve's policy decision adding to the rupee's list of external risks. A rate pause is widely expected, leaving markets focused on guidance on the rate outlook and whether further tightening remains on the table this year.
FALLING FX RESERVES India's foreign exchange reserves fell for a sixth consecutive week through October 16, declining by $5 billion to $721 billion.
Reserves are down more than $64 billion from their all-time high in the first week of September. Bankers have attributed part of the decline to the RBI's spot dollar sales to support the rupee, alongside sell/buy swaps used to manage rupee liquidity.

items.title: Israel markets see upside in Netanyahu defeat after three-year rally
items.author: Steven Scheer, Marc Jones
items.creator: Steven Scheer, Marc Jones
items.summary: Some investors see further upside if Netanyahu is defeated, potentially easing regional tensions.
items.body:
Israel's markets have soared despite three years of war and political turmoil, but some investors see further upside if the opposition defeats Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday’s election, potentially easing regional tensions and political risk.
Opinion polls point to a tight contest , with neither Netanyahu's ruling Likud bloc nor an opposition alliance centred on former military chief [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"] expected to secure the 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset needed to govern.
That raises the prospect of lengthy coalition negotiations or even another election. Since the October 7 Hamas attacks in 2023, the Tel Aviv stock market (.TASE) has soared 130%, far outpacing Wall Street's 80% gain, while the shekel has climbed 25% , one of the world's strongest currency performances.
Analysts attribute some of that strength to Israel's tech sector and the global AI boom, while defence spending, which has nearly doubled to around 8% of GDP, has also provided a boost.
With both Netanyahu and Eisenkot vowing to maintain pressure on Hamas and Iran, markets are focused on their broader policy differences. JPMorgan estimates the shekel could swing as much as 3% depending on the result.
An opposition victory that improves relations with Western allies and halts a judicial overhaul that sparked mass protests in 2023 could strengthen the currency, JPMorgan said, while another Netanyahu-led government could weaken it.
Billionaire investor [USN:L5N46B045 TEXT:"Bill Ackman"], while stopping short of backing a candidate, said a government without far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich would signal that Israel was "turning a new page," potentially helping rebuild its international credibility and expand the Abraham Accords with its neighbours.
IBI Investment House also expects an opposition victory to lift the markets. "From a capital markets perspective, this would likely be reflected in a decline in Israel's risk premium, appreciation pressure on the shekel, and a positive reaction in the local market," IBI's Chief Economist Rafi Gozlan said.
"The most significant issue is what the result will mean for the region," said Equity Bank's chief economic adviser Charlie Robertson. "If Netanyahu is reelected it might increase the chances of further escalation with Iran, whereas a defeat might be seen as lessening the tensions."
But the prospect of gains under an opposition government does not mean investors expect Israeli assets to suffer if Netanyahu remains in power. Stocks and bonds have proved remarkably resilient through years of war and political upheaval, and some investors remain confident in the economy regardless of the election outcome.
Union Investment's Sergey Dergachev has been buying Israeli bonds ahead of the election, betting the economy and companies he favours will remain fundamentally strong. "We are very constructive on Israeli credits going into the election," Dergachev said, adding that bonds were less prone to major swings and the region's intertwined conflicts should eventually ease.
RISKS REMAIN Despite the rally, foreign investors remain cautious. Copley Fund Research data show the share of global funds holding Israeli equities is at a record low, having fallen sharply since 2023.
TS Lombard's Christopher Granville cited central bank estimates that the war had cost the economy more than $55 billion by last year, equivalent to 8.6% in cumulative lost GDP growth.
Israel's fiscal position is another focus. Public debt has risen to nearly 70% of GDP, around 10 percentage points higher than in 2022, while the budget deficit is expected to remain around 4.5% of GDP, versus less than 2% before the conflict.
Central bank head Amir Yaron stressed last week the need to "preserve adequate fiscal policy space" given the Iran war.
FUNDAMENTAL STRENGTHS Like stocks, Israeli government bonds have rallied, returning about 30% over the last two years, more than double the main emerging market indexes.
The main risk for investors is an inconclusive result that prolongs political uncertainty, delaying budgets, reforms and investment, some investors believe.
That uncertainty can produce sharp short-term swings. Tel Aviv Stock Exchange research covering the last 10 elections found volatility in leading share indexes rose by as much as 45% in the weeks after voting compared with a typical week. But initial losses were typically recovered within a month, with the indexes posting an average gain of about 1.7%.
Over a longer horizon, the TA-125 returned an average 16.4% in the year following elections, compared with a long-term annual average of 11.5%, the research found. Political deadlock often weighed on stocks before voting, but the effects typically faded within months, said Nissan Avraham, an analyst at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's research unit.
That record supports the view that elections matter less for Israeli companies than many investors assume.
Lior Yochpaz, chief investment officer at insurance company Menora Mivtachim, said businesses have continued to thrive despite years of political upheaval, judicial overhaul proposals and regional conflict, helped by a relatively business-friendly environment.
For some investors, however, the more attractive election trade lies outside Israel. TT International's Jean-Charles Sambor said an opposition victory or weakened Netanyahu government could ease regional tensions and benefit Lebanese bonds.
"The best way to play it for us is through other Middle East countries, and for us Lebanon is a good proxy," Sambor said.

items.title: 中国百度と米リフト、27年ロンドンでロボタクシー商用化目指す
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Marissa Davison

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Marissa Davison

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - 米配車大手リフト傘下のフリーナウと中国ＩＴ大手・百度（バイドゥ）傘下のアポロ・ゴーは２２日、ロンドンでバイドゥの自動運転車「ＲＴ６」を公開し、２０２７年に同市で自動運転タクシー（ロボタクシー）事業の開始を目指すと発表した。

フリーナウとアポロ・ゴーは、この夏ロンドンで安全運転手を同乗させた車両の試験走行を開始しており、来年には完全無人走行車両を市内で走らせたいとしている。

米上院が米国内での中国製自動車の販売を恒久的に禁止する法案の可決に向けて動く中、リフトとバイドゥはロンドンでの提携を発表した。米国のこうした動きを背景に、欧州に注力する企業は増えている。

ロンドンではロボタクシー商用化を巡る競争が激化しており、英国の自動運転スタートアップのウェイブと米配車大手ウーバー・テクノロジーズは９月に、ロンドンでロボタクシー事業を、当初は安全運転手を乗せた状態で開始。米グーグルの親会社アルファベット傘下のロボタクシー企業、ウェイモも年内にロンドンにおける完全無人車両による配車サービスの開始を目標としている。

フリーナウの英事業責任者ダニー・オゴーマン氏は、ロンドンはスピードバンプが多く、道幅が狭いほか、制限速度が時速２０マイル（約３２キロ）の道路が多いため、試験には特に適していると指摘。「車両は、まるで自分が運転免許試験に合格しようとする時と同じように交通ルールを学ぶ段階にある」と説明した。

オゴーマン氏によると、フリーナウはロンドン交通局と緊密に連携しており、２６日の週にも規制ガイドラインが示される見込み。

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は続落し、前営業日比０．７６％（４７８円５０銭）安の６万２２１４円６６銭となった。今週は米大手ハイテク企業の決算発表や日米欧の中央銀行の金融政策決定会合といったイベントを複数控えており、手掛けにくさが意識された。人工知能（ＡＩ）・半導体関連株は軟調な銘柄が目立った一方、それ以外の銘柄では物色意欲もみられ、ＴＯＰＩＸはプラスだった。

・日経平均は小安く始まった後、プラスに切り返す場面もあり方向感欠く。

・アドバンテストなどＡＩ・半導体関連の主力株が売られ指数を下押し。

・東証プライム市場の６割近くが値上がりし、ＴＯＰＩＸは小幅プラス。

・原油価格が高止まりし、鉱業や石油・石炭製品、商社株などしっかり。

・円金利が上昇し、銀行や保険株に物色も。

・ブラジルのルラ大統領の当選確実が伝わり、ブラジル株に連動する上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）は急落。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは０．３４％高の３９７９．３４ポイントで午前の取引を終了。東証プライム市場の売買代金は３兆２４５４億２０００万円。

・東証３３業種で上昇したのは、鉱業、卸売、石油・石炭の２２業種、下落は非鉄金属、電気機器、機械の１１業種。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが９００銘柄（５７％）、値下がりは６０５銘柄（３８％）、変わらずは４８銘柄（３％）。

＜ちばぎんアセットマネジメント　調査部長　森田潤氏＞

「今週はイベントが目白押しでもあり、週初から積極的に動きにくく方向感を欠く」

「中銀会合はサプライズ見込まれず、波乱があるとすれば日米ハイテク決算か」

「ＴＯＰＩＸは節目の４０００ポイント割れでＡＩ以外に押し目買いも」

「ＡＩ株は足元で調整進んでおり、決算前に積極的に売る局面でもない」

items.title: IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The head of the International Energy Agency said on Monday that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war, which began in late February.
items.body:
The head of the International Energy Agency said on Monday that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war, which began in late February.
The conflict sharply tightened a market that had been projected to be in surplus this year, significantly disrupting global energy flows and pushing up oil benchmarks and refined product prices.
"I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol told the Singapore International Energy Week conference.
"So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today," he said.
More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sent Brent crude futures as high as $117 a barrel on Friday, the highest level in nearly six months.
The contract eased on Monday but was still trading about 59% above its pre-war level.
"Oil prices are flirting with $120 a barrel and the prices for products are even much higher," Birol told a press conference.
He declined to give a forecast for oil prices, but added: "I can tell you that the current price of oil is, for some countries, for example in Europe, maybe not so high and affordable. But in many parts of the world, having almost $120 oil prices is having a major impact on trade deficits."
WINTER CONCERNS Birol also raised concern about winter demand for some fuels, especially diesel, which is used in parts of the West for heating.
"I am worried on top of that for refined products because we are entering...winter season. Some parts of the world, where typically diesel demand goes high and several refineries are going through maintenance period."
"In Europe, we are facing a tough winter because European countries have decided to cut gas imports from Russia and with the additional problem now rising from the Iran war, namely Qatar and the Emirates not being able to export gas as they were before, will put significant pressure on gas markets."
Birol expects a "strong comeback" for the nuclear sector as a result of the current crisis.
The IEA's recent survey showed that 90 gigawatts of nuclear power plants are under construction and this is the highest in the last four decades, he added.

items.title: Week 7 injury roundup: Vikings’ Aaron Jones aggravates knee injury
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Minnesota running back Aaron Jones aggravated a left knee injury that he suffered earlier this season during the undefeated Vikings' 16-10 home win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
items.body:
Minnesota running back Aaron Jones aggravated a left knee injury that he suffered earlier this season during the undefeated Vikings' 16-10 home win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
Jones was seen heading straight for the blue medical tent following a hit at the end of a 17-yard run. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said after the game that Jones had the knee evaluated, and Pro Football Talk reported that the running back would undergo an MRI on Monday.
Jones sprained his left MCL in Week 2 against the Chicago Bears but has not missed a game. He finished with eight carries for 26 yards.
The Vikings did get back Jordan Mason (thumb) at running back for the first time since Week 1. He led the team with 68 yards on 15 carries.
--Carolina Panthers veteran right tackle Taylor Moton was carted off the field with a fractured left fibula during their 43-13 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Panthers coach Dave Canales acknowledged that Moton would be "out for a while" after the contest.
It was just Moton's second game since returning from a serious blood clot issue. He was hurt when teammate Rasheed Walker, the left tackle, fell across the back of his legs in the opening minute of the third quarter.
Moton held his left leg and punched the turf while waiting for trainers to come on the field.
"It was the fibula. There is a fracture there," Canales told reporters. "We'll have to get the full run-up to be able to give you the extent of the whole thing.
"But it was just sick for ‘T-Mo.' Working his way back, getting out there. Just kinda an end-of-the-play thing, guys just rolled up on him unexpectedly at that moment."
--Denver Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle exited his team's 30-16 road victory over the Arizona Cardinals with a chest injury.
The injury occurred on a reverse with under five minutes remaining. Waddle fumbled the pitch from quarterback Bo Nix and dove to recover the ball as Arizona's Josh Sweat landed on top of him. The receiver left for the locker room and didn't return.
Waddle (four catches, 48 yards on Sunday) was dealing with a chest injury during the week and was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He was a full participant on Friday and received no injury designation.
Broncos head coach Sean Payton criticized his own play call per the reverse in which Waddle was injured.
"Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call?" Payton said during his postgame press conference. "... It was awful. I'm sorry."
--The New York Giants came out of their 27-21 overtime win over the host Houston Texans with multiple injury concerns in the backfield.
Tyrone Tracy Jr. left in the first half with a hamstring injury, while Cam Skattebo also revealed he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard dash in overtime set up Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run to walk it off.
Skattebo had a career-high 124 yards as the Giants racked up 188 on the ground to support quarterback J.J. McCarthy in his first start for the team. The Giants get a chance to rest and recover with a bye in Week 8.
For the Texans, running back Woody Marks briefly left with an apparent left knee injury but returned to the game. Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said wide receiver Jaylin Noel had a turf toe injury, and Noel was seen wearing a boot.
--The banged-up Green Bay Packers' offensive line received two more blows as centers Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Jacob Monk (quad) made early exits.
Both players left the game in the first quarter of an eventual 20-17 road loss to the Detroit Lions. John Williams served as Green Bay's center the rest of the game.
Afterward, Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he wouldn't expect either Rhyan or Monk to be available on a quick turnaround for their next game Thursday against the Panthers.
The Packers already had lost tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (torn patellar tendon in his right knee) for the season, with starting guard Aaron Banks in and out of the lineup with multiple injuries.
Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (ankle) did not return after being hurt in the fourth quarter.
--In Paris, New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid sustained a concussion and running back CJ Donaldson hurt his shoulder during a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
--Seattle wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) exited early in the second half and did not return in the Seahawks' 20-3 home win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Starting left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) left in the fourth quarter, while running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) also went out early.
Shaheed caught two passes on three targets for 1 yard. Jones had five carries for 8 yards.
--Field Level Media
