items.title: ＧＭＯインターネットＧ株が急落、サイバー攻撃の損失補償と社長表明
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Shinichi Uchida　Noriyuki Hirata

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - ２６日の東京株式市場で...
items.body:
ＧＭＯインターネットＧ株が急落、サイバー攻撃の損失補償と社長表明
8:47 配信

写真は「サイバー攻撃」の文字イメージ。10月22日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Shinichi Uchida　Noriyuki Hirata

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - ２６日の東京株式市場で、ＧＭＯインターネットグループ株が急落した。ＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）自動売買サービスにサイバー攻撃があったことを受け、全ての顧客に見舞金５０００円を一律支払うほか、顧客が意図しない不正取引で生じた損失を補償する方針を打ち出したことで、業績への影響に対する不透明感を嫌気した売りが先行している。

熊谷正寿代表は２５日、不正アクセスにより生じた顧客の損失はＧＭＯインターネットが確認した上で補償すると自身のブログで表明した。取引所が返金に応じない場合でも、対象となる損失の全額を支払うとしている。同社によると、一部のユーザーから身に覚えのない取引が行われたとの報告が寄せられているという。

熊谷氏は、顧客の資産や情報を危険にさらす事態を招いた事実を「極めて重く受け止めている」とし、一律５０００円の見舞金は「初動の誠意の印」と説明。財務への影響などは見通しが立ち次第報告するとした。セキュリティーの課題が事前に現場へ指摘され対策を進めながらも、 対応の深さとスピードが十分ではなく、その間隙を突かれたとした。また、人工知能（ＡＩ）技術の進化に伴い攻撃者のコストが劇的に低下し、脅威が急速に深刻化しているとも訴えた。

ＧＭＯによると、攻撃者とみられる相手から金銭を要求されており、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡も受けているという。要求には応じない方針で、警察などと連携して対応するとしている。２４日には、先制的に相手を無力化する「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を政府に緊急要請したことも発表した。

ＧＭＯは今月１９日、顧客からの問い合わせを受けて調査を開始した。２０日にサービスの一部顧客のサーバー環境への不正なプログラムの設置を確認し、２１日には被害拡大防止のため全プランのサーバーを順次停止した。顧客から取引口座での身に覚えのない操作などの報告があり、２２日に警察へ相談した。

Manchester United is eyeing replacements for Michael Carrick as the former club legend's future as a manager is in serious doubt following a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth on Sunday, sources told ESPN. Man United's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford continues to pile up pressure and losses on Carrick, who was roped in for a full-time deal after leading multi-time Premier League champions to the UEFA Champions League after a rocky start to their league campaign, replacing Ruben Amorim as an interim manager before taking up the full-time task ahead of the 2026-27 season.
It was the second poor result of the week for the Red Devils, having lost to UEFA Champions League debutants Como by 4-1 on Wednesday. Manchester United are struggling to keep themselves afloat in the points table, sitting at 16th spot, just a point above the relegation zone. They have gone eight games without a win across all competitions.
Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann, both currently not roped in by any team, are among top contenders to take Carrikc's spot. Former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna impressed in talks with United's hierarchy back in summer-2024 before the club decided to retain Erik ten Hag.
Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would be open to talks if contacted by Premier League giants. Manchester United, as per sources, spent time doing research on coaches before handing a two-year deal to Carrick after a successful interim spell. It is also understood that the club is prepared for Carrick's departure.
After the loss to Bournemouth, Carrick was questioned about his future, to which he replied, "I totally understand the situation," he said. "I am not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal," he signed off. (ANI)

items.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat in historic election win for student protest movement
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Aleksandar Vucic has held power in Serbia since 2014, and his defeat heralds a new political era for the Balkan country.
items.body:

Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat in historic election win for student protest movement

Aleksandar Vucic has held power in Serbia since 2014, and his defeat heralds a new political era for the Balkan country.

Serbia's former President and the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) prime ministerial candidate Aleksandar Vucic concedes defeat during the parliamentary election in Belgrade, Serbia, on Oct 25, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Zorana Jevtic)

FAST

BELGRADE: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led protest movement in a historic election on Sunday (Oct 25) that ends his long grip on power and heralds a new political era in the Balkan country.
Vucic, a populist and nationalist, has dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president since 2014.
But he called snap elections in September after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.
"It is clear that we have lost these elections, the Student List has won," Vucic said in a televised speech.

Within moments of his announcement, the streets of Belgrade erupted in celebration. Tens of thousands of people thronged along the city's main boulevards, with cars honking, people dancing and students shouting "victory" and "he's done".
The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of about 6 million people and is reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban in April. It may also offer a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have taken to the streets in recent weeks to protest, in some cases violently, against poor education standards and a lack of prospects.
Vucic said the students would have between 135 and 140 seats in the 250-seat parliament and that his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) would have 105, based on preliminary results.
"Dear Serbia, tonight the voice of the people is being heard," said Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, speaking on behalf of the students at their headquarters.
"Tonight we celebrate victory, tomorrow we build the future."
European leaders and officials congratulated the Student List on its victory, among them President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen and European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos.
"We stand ready to ... work together to advance Serbia's future in the European Union," von der Leyen wrote on X.
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar assured the students of his country's support.

Supporters of the electoral list "Student List - Students Win" celebrate after Aleksandar Vucic, Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) prime ministerial candidate, conceded defeat in the parliamentary election in Belgrade, Serbia, on Oct 25, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Marko Djurica)

RECORD TURNOUT SPURS STUDENTS TO VICTORY Lines snaked from polling stations in cities and towns across the country earlier in the day, and even Vucic waited for nearly two hours to vote in Belgrade. Pollsters and the election commission put turnout close to 70 per cent, the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992.
"(The turnout) did not surprise me because there was a large and strong mass that has formed throughout the past two years," said voter Katarina Petrovic.
Vucic, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, was a strong incumbent and few in the student protest movement dared believe he would concede so fast.
Supporters credit him with modernising Serbia's economy and building new highways, railways, schools and hospitals.
"Some businessmen, some people will leave us but our structure is firm, we are very united, very strong, we are used to being in the opposition," Vucic said.
UNCERTAINTY OVER THE STUDENTS' CANDIDATES Much remains unclear about how the student-backed candidates will fare.
Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, who was in tears after Vucic's announcement.
However, it is unclear who will be prime minister and enact the students' domestic agenda, which aims to root out graft and improve schooling. Political analysts predict some kind of purge of Vucic allies in the police, security services and ministries. But the students have been quieter on their international ambitions.
As Vucic did for years, they will have to juggle relations with China, a major investor, Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, and the European Union, Serbia's largest trading partner.
"The biggest uncertainty is ... who is going to lead the government, who will be the key ministers, and how they will operate based on the promises they made to fight corruption, to reintroduce the rule of law, but also to re-establish Serbia's position in foreign policy," said Radivoje Grujic, a Warsaw-based election consultant.
PROTEST MOVEMENT INCREASED PRESSURE The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster started small but quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say repression worsened in the period since.
Vucic and the SNS repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He has said the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss.
Meanwhile, on the streets of Belgrade, a traditional brass band struck up, and a group including a man in a "students are champions" jumper floated balloons in the shape of the number 3, representing the number of the students' list of candidates.
"We will drink a beer to celebrate, we will get drunk, we are so happy, I have no words to describe how much," said Andjela, a student who was with a group of friends.
Dejan Soskic, a former central bank governor and a candidate of the Student List, called on people to maintain order and peace, and thanked voters for their civilised conduct during the electoral process.

Source: Reuters/dy

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Toby Sterling

[アムステルダム ２３日 ロイター] - ２つの重大な脆弱性が見つかったプログラミング言語...
items.body:
脆弱性発見のＰＨＰ、支援財団常勤スタッフは1人だけ＝代表
8:27 配信

写真は「PHPコード」のイメージ。10月22日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Toby Sterling

[アムステルダム ２３日 ロイター] - ２つの重大な脆弱性が見つかったプログラミング言語「ＰＨＰ」を支援し、世界中のウェブサイトの最大７割で利用されているとされる非営利団体（ＮＰＯ）「ＰＨＰ財団」のエリザベス・バロン事務局長は２３日、同財団がごくわずかな予算で運営されているとメールでの取材に答えた。

バロン氏は「常勤スタッフは（私のみの）１人で、残りの１４人は主にパートタイムの契約社員」だと回答した。理事は無報酬のボランティアであり、資金は寄付や助成金によって賄われている。

同財団は米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のオープンＡＩや、ともにサイバーセキュリティーの新興企業Ｗｉｚ（ウィズ）、カリフなどの企業や外部の研究者と連携し、セキュリティー上の欠陥を調査するとともに、２１日に公開したパッチを含めた修正作業に当たっている。

セキュリティー企業クラウドフレアは数百万件のハッキングがあったと報告した。だがバロン氏は、脆弱性が公表される前や、パッチが適用されたサイトでハッカーが情報を盗み出した証拠は把握していないと説明。「この問題について緊密に連携しているオープンＡＩ、ウィズ、カリフのいずれからも、パッチが適用されたシステムに関して問題の報告は受けていない」と答えた。

ＰＨＰ財団にとってＡＩはもろ刃の剣となっている。ＡＩは１０年間も続いていた欠陥を発見するのを助け、バロン氏はプログラマーの作業効率も向上させたと紹介した。

メンテナンスの作業負荷も増大させている。同財団には１年前の２倍弱のコード変更提案が寄せられているが、「貢献者の数は２倍にはなっていない」と指摘。貢献内容やバグの報告の審査には「膨大な人的リソースと経験」が必要となると解説した。

バロン氏は、２つの脆弱性が見つかったことに伴う混乱は企業や政府がいかにＰＨＰ財団に依存しているのかを浮き彫りにしたとして「その依存度を考えると、ＰＨＰへの資金提供が著しく不足していることは明らかだ」と訴えた。

items.title: Oil drops from near six-month highs on hopes Iran war hostilities to ease
items.author: Mohi Narayan, Colleen Howe
items.creator: Mohi Narayan, Colleen Howe
items.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging last week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary.
items.body:
Oil prices fell on Monday after surging last week to near six-month highs, amid hopes of easing hostilities between the United States and Iran, although persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary.
US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $2.23, or 2.16%, at $101.04 per barrel by 0426 GMT. Brent crude futures were down $2.21, or 1.89%, at $114.51.
On Friday, prices [USN:L1N46903W TEXT:"settled"] nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6% and WTI ended 2.3% higher.
On Sunday, Qatari [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"mediators"] traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States, an official briefed on the situation said.
"Concerns over renewed military hostilities in the Middle East, which drove much of last week’s crude rally, have eased this morning, but the reprieve may prove temporary," said Vandana Hari, founder of oil market analysis provider Vanda Insights.
Hari said US President Donald Trump has not dispelled market expectations that strikes on Iran could still follow after the November 3 midterm elections.
"We therefore expect volatility to remain elevated, with risks still skewed to the upside," she added.
Despite the mediation talks, attacks continued over the weekend with the Iran-backed Houthis saying they struck an airport and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones.
The effects of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28 continue to reverberate as companies adjust to the disruptions of [USN:L1N4690RP TEXT:"commercial shipping"] through the key Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait caused by the conflict.
On Monday, the energy ministers from Saudi Arabia and Singapore said state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco will start [USN:L2N46C022 TEXT:"storing"] crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, to shore up the resilience of Aramco's supply chain in the region.
"While supply risks surrounding the Strait of Hormuz remain firmly entrenched, the current pullback appears more reflective of position adjustments and risk management rather than any meaningful improvement in the underlying supply situation," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insight at Phillip Nova.
The [USN:P8N3RS06K TEXT:"head"] of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, reinforced the concerns about the supply situation, saying on Monday at an industry event in Singapore that he does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to where they were before the Iran war.

BEIJING, Oct 26 : Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.
US crude futures were down $1.60, or 1.55 per cent, at $101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures were down $1.56 or 1.34 per cent at $115.16.
Prices had settled nearly $3 higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6 per cent and WTI ended 2.3 per cent higher.
Attacks continued over the weekend with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones.
The top oil exporter restarted partial operations at its main airport on Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks even as the militant group vowed to keep targeting the facility.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Belgrade in rapture as Serbian students topple Vucic in historic election
items.author: Edward Mcallister, Kirsten Donovan, Aleksandar Vasovic
items.creator: Edward Mcallister, Kirsten Donovan, Aleksandar Vasovic
items.summary: It was the culmination of a two-year protest movement that called for Vucic to step down.
items.body:
Trams and traffic halted by crowds. Tens of thousands of people choking the city's main boulevards; the air thick with smoke; a man on a car waving a flare.
Familiar-sounding scenes after a month of sometimes violent protests across European cities as students take to the streets calling for better education standards and better prospects.
Except, on Sunday night in Serbia's capital Belgrade, students were not protesting but celebrating an election victory after long-time ruler Aleksandar Vucic [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"conceded defeat"] to a student-backed list of candidates in parliamentary elections.
It was the culmination of a two-year, [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"peaceful protest movement"] that called for Vucic to step down and an end to what they said is rampant corruption in the Balkan country - a charge Vucic denies.
The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and shows what power younger generation have when they are able to harness widespread discontent.
"That is the best thing that happened in my life. We will now breathe freely," said Milica, a law student.
Vucic had ruled as prime minister or president since 2014, and oversaw a period of strong economic growth, but he faced growing opposition from student-led protests after the collapse of a railway station awning killed 16 people in November 2024.
Tomorrow, the disparate group of 250 student-backed candidates will have to turn towards ruling, but Sunday evening was a time to party.
At their headquarters, the unknown candidates, many of them lawyers, professors, actors or farmers, hugged and cheered in near disbelief at what they had achieved.
"The people have won! The people defeated a dictator! The people will lead Serbia!" said Nebojsa Cosic while waving a flag on the street.

Oct 25 : AI model Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization, Anthropic said in a statement on Sunday.
• "Claude didn't access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records," Anthropic said, adding that it has since taken steps to block these kinds of actions.
• Anthropic said in a blog post earlier this month it found examples of Claude "working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee" and some of these cases involved websites run by US government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels.
• The secretary of state's office in Georgia did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
• Axios first reported the unauthorized action by Claude.

items.title: アウディＣＥＯ、トランプ氏発表の米新工場建設計画を正当化
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Bo Erickson　David Shepardson　Rachel More

[ペリー（米ジョージア州）／ベルリン...
items.body:
アウディＣＥＯ、トランプ氏発表の米新工場建設計画を正当化
7:36 配信

アウディのロゴ。2025年2月26日、オランダのネイメーヘンで撮影。REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw

Bo Erickson　David Shepardson　Rachel More

[ペリー（米ジョージア州）／ベルリン ２５日 ロイター] - ドイツ自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）傘下アウディのゲルノート・デルナー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２５日、トランプ米大統領が発表した同社による米南部ジョージア州での４０億ドル（約５８００億円）規模の新工場建設計画について「数カ月にわたる慎重な計画と集中的な交渉を経た決定だ」と述べ、妥当な判断だと強調した。投資計画の実施にはＶＷ監査役会の最終承認が必要となる。

デルナー氏は２４日、ジョージア州ペリーで開かれたトランプ大統領の集会に登壇。トランプ氏はアウディが同州に年産２０万台規模のＳＵＶ（スポーツタイプ多目的車）組立工場を建設する計画だと明らかにした。

デルナー氏は記者団に「米大統領から招待を受ければ応じる。投資先の国とその職務に敬意を示すためだ」と語っていた。

ジョージア州では１１月３日の中間選挙の上院選と知事選が接戦となっており、トランプ氏は自らの自動車関税政策が米経済と国内製造業を押し上げていると有権者に訴えている。

アウディによると、自動車や鉄鋼、アルミニウム、部品に対するトランプ政権の関税措置により、同社は昨年約１２億ユーロ（１４億ドル）の負担を強いられた。同社は米国向け車両を欧州とメキシコから輸入している。デルナー氏はそうした関税の軽減措置が含まれるかどうかなど米国との合意内容の詳細については明らかにしなかった。

ドイツ最大の産業別労働組合ＩＧメタルの報道担当者は、デルナー氏が選挙期間中にトランプ氏との協調姿勢を示したことについて「理解し難い。トランプ氏はドイツの自動車産業を含む国内経済を弱体化させようとしていることを隠していない」と批判した。

ＩＧメタル委員長でＶＷ監査役会副会長を務めるクリスティアーネ・ベナー氏は、新工場建設による米市場での競争力強化は「正しく必要なことだ」と評価した一方で「特にドイツ国内の各拠点で働く従業員の将来について明確な見通しを示す必要がある」と指摘した。

ＶＷ第２位株主のニーダーザクセン州のリース州首相は、米国での生産拡大はドイツ国内の雇用維持につながれば好機だとの見方を示すとともに「米国での成長はドイツ国内の雇用と付加価値創出を確保するものでなければならず、置き換えになってはならない」と述べた。

アウディによると、新工場によって約４５００人の雇用が創出される見込み。建設は来年開始し、生産は２０３０年代初頭に始まる予定だ。

ロイターが米政府当局者の話として報じたところでは、新工場では「Ｑ７」「Ｑ８」「Ｑ９」の各ＳＵＶを組み立てる計画。またアウディは隣接するサウスカロライナ州でも年２万５０００台を生産する方針で、一部車種は欧州から移管され、輸出にも充てられる見通しという。

これらの車両は、サウスカロライナ州ブライスウッドで建設中のＶＷ傘下ブランド「スカウト・モーターズ」の総額２０億ドルの工場で組み立てられる予定だ。

ＶＷのオリバー・ブルーメＣＥＯは「北米地域を収益性の高い成長市場と位置付けている。米国内のアウディ新工場はその条件をさらに整える形になる」と述べた。

items.title: スペースＸ、400億ドル調達　マスク氏「ネオクラウド再編」予測
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２５日 ロイター] - 米宇宙関連企業スペースＸのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２５日、画像処理装置（ＧＰ...
items.body:
スペースＸ、400億ドル調達　マスク氏「ネオクラウド再編」予測
7:28 配信

米宇宙関連企業スペースＸのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）。2026年10月8日、米首都ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Evan Vucci/File Photo/File Photo

[２５日 ロイター] - 米宇宙関連企業スペースＸのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２５日、画像処理装置（ＧＰＵ）の購入に向けた４００億ドルの債務による資金調達を完了したとＸで明らかにした。

同社の格付けが投資適格級であることや、スターリンクの衛星インターネット事業およびロケット打ち上げ事業による収入が寄与したと説明した。

ただ、資金調達を「完了した」という発言の意味や、投資家が債務の価格条件に合意したかどうかは、投稿からは直ちに明らかにならなかった。 

マスク氏は「これは主に（２０２７年）第１・四半期および第２・四半期に納入されるＧＰＵの購入に向けた早期償還可能な債務だ。この四半期（２６年第４・四半期）に大きな影響を与えるものではない」と述べた。

ブレット・ジョンセン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）によると、同社は第４・四半期の設備投資を３５０億─４００億ドルと見込んでいる。

スペースＸが人工知能（ＡＩ）向けのエヌビディア製半導体を購入するため、４００億ドルの資金調達を目指していることはロイターが既に報じていた。

テクノロジー各社がＡＩ開発に必要な先端半導体の確保と演算インフラの構築を競う中、今回の資金調達は、ＡＩブームに伴う巨額の資金需要を浮き彫りにしている。

マスク氏は、債務市場では「ＡＩデータセンター以外から多額の収入を得ていない企業は、資金調達の道をほぼ完全に閉ざされている」と述べた。

このため、ＡＩ向けクラウドサービスに特化した「ネオクラウド」企業の間で大規模な再編や経営破綻が起きると予測。その後、スペースＸがネオクラウド企業を買収することはないとし、「無意味だ」と述べた。

幅広い業種にサービスを提供する大手クラウド企業とは異なり、ネビウスやコアウィーブなどのネオクラウド企業は、主にテクノロジー企業を顧客とし、ＡＩ技術向けに特化した演算能力を提供している。

スペースＸの第３・四半期（７―９月期）の売上高は前年同期の２．６１倍の１４５億８０００万ドルに達した。設備投資は３倍の１９６億ドルに膨らみ、演算インフラへの支出がかさんだ。

ＡＩ関連売上高は約１０倍の７５億６０００万ドルに急増し、ＡＩへの巨額投資が成果を上げつつあることを、これまでで最も明確に示した。

スペースＸと、同じくマスク氏がＣＥＯを務めるテスラによる半導体製造合弁事業「テラファブ」は２８年第３・四半期までに量産開始を目指している。来年５月または６月ごろに最初の試験用半導体の生産に乗り出す見込みだ。

Oct 26 : NEXTDC CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments last week.
Here are some details:
• The company said the board has withdrawn the resolution proposing an approval of grant of performance rights and restricted rights to the CEO under the fiscal 2027 long term incentive plan.
• Current Chairman Douglas Flynn has reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period.

• The board expects to appoint two new non-executive directors in the first calendar quarter of 2027, NEXTDC added.
• The company said the board has also withdrawn the resolution seeking shareholder approval to increase the maximum aggregate annual remuneration of non-executive directors by A$300,000 ($210,660), with the incumbent non-executive directors also agreeing to an immediate voluntary 10 per cent reduction in their current fees.
• Last week, NEXTDC said delays to electricity network upgrades at one of its major Melbourne projects would mean about A$140 million worth of contracted customer revenue this financial year would be deferred.
• The firm is set to hold its annual general meeting on November 20.
($1 = 1.4241 Australian dollars)

items.body:
"Most Tests feel like finals": Aussie keeper-batter Carey ahead of series decider against South Africa The Aussies head into the fixture sitting on top of the World Test Championship standings and with the number one ranking in Test cricket, but will lose both mantles if they succumb to a defeat against the Proteas in the series deciding Test at Newlands. Another poor showing with the bat, including a 99 all out in the first innings and skipper Temba Bavuma's resilient 179 were the highlights as Proteas made a comeback at Gqeberha with an innings win.

AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Australian wicketkeeper Alex Carey expressed the importance of the upcoming Test matches ahead of the final Test against South Africa, with plenty of important ICC World Test Championship points at stake. The Aussies head into the fixture sitting on top of the World Test Championship standings and with the number one ranking in Test cricket, but will lose both mantles if they succumb to a defeat against the Proteas in the series-deciding Test at Newlands. Another poor showing with the bat, including a 99 all out in the first innings and skipper Temba Bavuma's resilient 179, were the highlights as Proteas made a comeback at Gqeberha with an innings win.
But rather than dwell on what the consequences would look like should Australia fall to South Africa in the third Test, Carey has instead decided to focus on the positives and concentrate on ensuring the team gets their preparation right so the result in Cape Town takes care of itself. "As a group, we really believe in what we can achieve," Carey told reporters in Cape Town, as quoted by ICC.
"If that is after this Test we are ranked number one, or we are not. I think we know what we are capable of when we certainly get it right." "So we would not look too far ahead. And I know it is probably a little bit cliché, but we have got to get our preparation right going into this Test match, and then hopefully things can take care of themselves there and not look at the end result," he continued.
If the Aussies can taste success in the third Test, then it will boost their chances of earning a place at next year's World Test Championship Final, with the side scheduled to take on New Zealand in four Tests later this year before a five-match series in India for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in January and February of 2027. With so much to play for in the coming months, Carey suggested the result in every Test will be crucial for his side with the stakes raised under the World Test Championship cycle.
"I think most Test matches feel like finals," Carey admitted. "You do not take any for granted, and you want to win every single one of them, as you know the significance of them.
"You know the point system around the World Test Championship. So, as a playing group, I think it is really important for us to understand the process of every game that we go into and try to nail that. And this one, again, is no different," he signed off. (ANI)

items.title: Real Madrid defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou to halve gap to LaLiga leaders
items.author: Ruairidh Barlow
items.creator: Ruairidh Barlow
items.summary: Kylian Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended.
items.body:
Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe.
Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points.
"It was the most difficult match, against the highest quality opponent, one that had only won in the league," Mourinho told reporters. "For us, it's the victory with the most impressive performance."
Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve.
Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's [USN:L6N46B0AT TEXT:"game plan"] was functioning better than his own.
In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net.
Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range.
It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner.
Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing.
Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward.
That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net.
"It's two defeats and we're not happy," Flick told reporters. "We're disappointed. We lacked freshness."
The defeat ended Barcelona's nine-match winning start to the league campaign and came days after a 4-2 [USN:L6N4661CR TEXT:"Champions League defeat"] by Paris St Germain.
Flick pointed to a demanding run of travel as a factor behind his side's drop in energy levels.
"These past few weeks haven't been easy. You only see the matches, but being on a plane for three hours to Seville, returning to the hotel, then going to Paris; it's a lot," he said.
"I don't want to talk about this when we lose. It's better when we win, and I won't accept excuses."
Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points.
Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

items.title: Lars Eller scores first goal with Panthers in narrow win over Blackhawks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
items.body:
Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
Panthers goaltender Akira Schmid stopped 19 shots as Florida snapped a two-game losing streak. Schmid turned aside Cole Smith on a breakaway with 5:45 to keep the game tied at 2.
Eller netted his first goal of the season at 17:37 of the third period as the Panthers caught the Blackhawks in a line change. Eller took a long pass from Aaron Ekblad just inside the blue line, weaved down the right side and ripped a wrist shot from the circle past Chicago goaltender Spencer Knight.
For the 37-old-year Eller, it was also his first goal as a member of the Florida Panthers. He started his NHL career with the St. Louis Blues in the 2009-10 season and has played for the Montreal Canadiens (2010-16), Washington Capitals (2016-23, 2024-25), Colorado Avalanche (2023), Pittsburgh Penguins (2023-25) and Ottawa Senators (2025-26).
Special-teams struggles hurt the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-7 on the power play while also failing to capitalize on other chances at even strength. Knight made 30 saves.
Chicago managed just six shots in the first period, but one of the club's early attempts provided a 1-0 lead.
Ryan Greene tracked a puck that bounced at the top of the crease and into the air and batted it past Schmid and into the net. Andrew Mangiapane earned the primary assist in his return to the lineup; the forward had been out since sustaining a lower-body injury in the club's season opener on Sept. 29.
Florida tied the game just over four minutes later, as Vilmanis backhanded a loose puck past Knight after the backstop made a save on Sam Reinhart.
The Panthers took a 2-1 lead on Matthew Tkachuk's power-play goal at 14:21 of the first. Tkachuk deflected Seth Jones' shot from the point just five seconds into the man advantage.
Chicago netted the equalizer at 11:15 of the second period when Roman Kantserov took a Patrick Kane feed from behind the net and scored on a wrist shot from the right circle.
Florida limited Chicago to one shot on goal during a four-minute power-play early in the second period after Carter Verhaeghe was whistled for a high-sticking double minor against the Blackhawks' Wyatt Kaiser.
Verhaeghe sent a wrist shot off the crossbar on a breakaway moments after springing from the penalty box.
The Blackhawks fell to 2-4-0 on a seven-game homestand that is set to conclude with Tuesday's visit from the Los Angeles Kings.
--Field Level Media

items.title: North Korea-South Korea tensions high as letters lodged with UN, howitzer spotted
items.author: Hongji Kim, Kyu-Seok Shim, Joyce Lee
items.creator: Hongji Kim, Kyu-Seok Shim, Joyce Lee
items.summary: Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident, and after a North Korean howitzer was spotted close to the border.
items.body:
Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident, and after a North Korean howitzer was spotted close to the border.
A Reuters witness at an observatory in South Korea overlooking the heavily armed border on Monday confirmed the presence of a North Korean artillery piece positioned in clear view near the frontier.
South Korea's Yonhap news agency on Sunday identified the weapon as a self-propelled 122-mm howitzer, saying its deployment near the border marked a rare public display of such artillery.
Reuters also observed three North Korean armored vehicles with their gun barrels pointed south, as well as about 20 to 30 North Korean soldiers carrying out fencing work inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ).
"It is highly unusual (for North Korea) to expose its self-propelled artillery so conspicuously,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University in Seoul.
"By deliberately displaying it, North Korea is signalling through action, not words, that it intends to enforce its border policy through force rather than dialogue or negotiation."
It is also warning South Korea to exercise caution about escalating border friction, with the intention to prevent an accidental clash, he added.
North Korean state media KCNA reported that in the letter sent on Sunday, the country's UN representative said Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang's border construction as a military incursion.
North Korea warned in the letter that violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence measures and that South Korea would be "wholly accountable for all the ensuing consequences."
PHOTOS ALSO SHOW NORTH KOREAN DRILLS The letter is a response to a South Korean letter to the Security Council last week, which said a September 21 blast in the DMZ was planted by North Korean troops and constituted a violation of the Korean War Armistice Agreement.
The UN Command, which oversees the DMZ, has said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility.
A spokesperson for South Korea's Unification Ministry said on Monday that the North Korean letter appears to repeat North Korea's existing position and seeks to justify its so-called border line marking work.
The ministry had no separate comment on the placement of the howitzer. Seoul has [USN:L1N46905T TEXT:"proposed"] dialogue with North Korea to defuse border tensions.
North Korea's letter also repeated accusations that South Korea had opened fire on North Korean personnel, calling that a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat or use of force against another state's territorial integrity.
Seoul has said its military issues warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to send North Korean soldiers back across the line when they cross the military demarcation line (MDL), which bisects the DMZ.
North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years.
The Yonhap report cited photographs taken from an observatory in the South Korean border city of Gimpo that appeared to show the howitzer as well as North Korean troops conducting drills on the coast of Kaepung county, about 1.5 km (1 mile) from the observatory.
In 2015, there was a similar incident in which South Korean troops were injured by North Korean mines. Then, Seoul resumed anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts across the DMZ, triggering a military standoff. After North Korea expressed regret, the standoff ended with a high-level inter-Korean agreement.

items.title: NFL roundup: Falcons harass 49ers into first loss of 2026
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss.
items.body:
Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss.
Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards while rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels picked off a pass and recovered a fumble in the fourth quarter for the Falcons (3-4), who won their first home game of the season. Nick Folk added three field goals.
Brock Purdy hit 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for the 49ers (6-1). Christian McCaffrey rushed for 39 yards and one touchdown while catching six passes for 61 yards.
The 49ers built a 14-3 lead on Kaelon Black's 30-yard touchdown run on the first play of the second quarter, but the Falcons responded with 23 unanswered points as Penix completed touchdown strikes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts Sr. and Drake London.
Seahawks 20, Chiefs 3
Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 yards and a score as host Seattle defeated Kansas City, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.
Wilson had 24 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown run around the left end with 3:47 remaining to clinch the victory for the defending Super Bowl champions. Sam Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards with one touchdown and one interception for the Seahawks (4-3).
NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III, who was the MVP of the Seahawks' 29-13 Super Bowl victory against New England before signing with Kansas City as a free agent in the offseason, was limited to 36 yards on 14 carries in his return to Seattle. Patrick Mahomes was 19-of-33 passing for 165 yards with an interception for the Chiefs (5-1), who had just 213 yards of total offense to the Seahawks' 410.
Giants 27, Titans 21 (OT)
Devin Singletary ran for a 30-yard touchdown to defeat his former team and propel New York to the walkoff victory over host Houston.
J.J. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards to win his debut start for the Giants (4-2-1) and his fifth consecutive start overall. Cam Skattebo had 17 carries for 124 yards, including a 42-yard run the play before Singletary's game-winner, and Malik Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards.
C.J. Stroud completed 17 of 28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (2-5), who dropped to 0-4 at home. Woody Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and tight end Dalton Schultz had five catches for 45 yards. Stroud's 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds left forced overtime.
Steelers 16, Saints 10
Aaron Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown passes list, Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Pittsburgh defeated New Orleans in the first NFL game played in Paris.
The Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game after shutting out the Saints (2-5) in the second half in Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of Paris. Rodgers broke a tie with Manning for third place on the all-time list when he completed his 540th career touchdown pass to Darnell Washington in the second quarter.
Tyler Shough passed for 278 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Saints, who rushed for just 18 yards -- 130 fewer than Pittsburgh.
Browns 27, Titans 24
Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of a victory over Tennessee in Nashville.
After Tennessee tied it 24-24 with 58 seconds remaining on Tony Pollard's third touchdown of the day, Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards with 28 seconds left. Szmyt, who missed from 43 yards in the fourth quarter, booted the winner to keep the Browns (5-2) atop the AFC North.
Watson eclipsed 300 yards for the first time with the Browns as he completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception. He also rushed for a score. For the Titans (1-6), Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards.
Dolphins 28, Jets 25
Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help Miami pick up its first win, beating New York in East Rutherford, N.J.
Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without an interception and rushed for 37 yards on eight attempts to help give head coach Jeff Hafley his first NFL victory. Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries as the Dolphins (1-5) rushed for 156 yards overall.
The Jets (2-5) lost for the fifth time in six games and lost their eighth consecutive game against an AFC East opponent. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Smith's third touchdown pass was a 12-yarder to Mason Taylor, who caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns.
Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13
Bucky Irving rushed for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown and Tampa Bay blasted mistake-prone Carolina in Charlotte.
Baker Mayfield was back at quarterback for the Buccaneers (2-5) after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb and had an easy return while completing 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and one touchdown.
The Panthers (3-3) committed four turnovers and missed an extra-point kick. Bryce Young was 14-of-27 passing for 163 yards with two interceptions and a touchdown, while losing a fumble.
Vikings 16, Colts 10
Kyler Murray passed for 150 yards and a touchdown, and safety Harrison Smith made an interception in the final minutes to preserve a Minnesota victory over Indianapolis in Minneapolis.
T.J. Hockenson had the go-ahead touchdown catch for the Vikings (6-0) early in the fourth quarter. Jordan Mason had a team-high 68 rushing yards, and Justin Jefferson caught four passes for 44 yards on seven targets. Will Reichard made three of four field goal attempts.
Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and a touchdown to lead the Colts (2-5). Daniel Jones completed 13 of 22 yards for 108 yards and an interception. Indianapolis fell despite converting 9-of-16 third- and fourth-down chances.
Bengals 35, Ravens 13
Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and Cincinnati scored 35 unanswered points to record a victory over host Baltimore.
Burrow completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards while leading five touchdown drives in the half as the Bengals (4-2) overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample also caught touchdown passes and Samaje Perine rushed for a score.
Lamar Jackson (ankle) missed his third straight game for the Ravens (4-3). Tyler "Snoop" Huntley completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards and one score for Baltimore, which blew a double-digit lead for the second straight week.
Broncos 30, Cardinals 16
Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass and ran 62 yards for another, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey also scored TDs, and Denver topped Arizona in Glendale, Ariz.
Nix finished 15-for-29 passing for 222 yards and also rushed for 73 yards for the Broncos (5-2), who have won three in a row and won three of four games against NFC West opponents.
Jacoby Brissett finished 27-for-48 passing for 272 yards and a touchdown pass to Trey McBride, who had 10 receptions for 111 yards for the Cardinals. Arizona (2-5) has lost 10 straight home games dating back to Sept. 14, 2025.
Rams 35, Raiders 21
Matthew Stafford threw for three touchdowns and visiting Los Angeles built a 28-3 second-quarter lead on its way to victory against slumping Las Vegas.
Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards and an interception as the Rams (3-4) snapped a two-game losing streak. Kyren Williams (16 rushes, 99 yards) and Blake Corum (17 attempts, 93 yards) each scored a touchdown and contributed to Los Angeles' 386 yards of offense.
Kirk Cousins hit 26 of 44 throws for 295 yards and two touchdowns, but it wasn't enough as the Raiders (3-4) dropped their fourth straight game. Las Vegas managed just 48 yards on 17 carries and abandoned the run for most of the second half.
Lions 20, Packers 17
Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give host Detroit a victory over Green Bay and snap the Packers' three-game winning streak.
The Lions' Jared Goff passed for 303 yards and two touchdowns, both to Jameson Williams. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 153 yards and Williams hauled in five for 91 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries for Detroit (4-2).
Jordan Love passed for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception for Green Bay (4-3). Running back Josh Jacobs, activated off the NFL commissioner's exempt list, rushed for 36 yards and caught five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown in his season debut.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix but must wait for title
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion.
items.body:
Kimi Antonelli delivered a dominant US Grand Prix victory for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion with four rounds to spare in Mexico next weekend.
The 20-year-old Italian did all he could to put the championship out of reach of his rivals in Texas but Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes teammate George Russell did just enough to delay the inevitable with fourth and eighth respectively.
Antonelli now needs to score only two points -- a ninth place -- in Mexico City to be sure of the title even if Russell wins.
"It was the result we needed and the whole team deserve it so much," he said of his first win since Spain last month. "I know we're very close. We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon".
LECLERC SECOND AND VERSTAPPEN THIRD Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished second, 13.078 seconds behind, in Sunday's race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with Red Bull's Max Verstappen third and helped by a late virtual safety car that slowed a chasing Hamilton who finished one second down the road.
The win from pole position on a one-stop strategy was Antonelli's ninth in of the season and he now leads Russell by 123 points, and Hamilton by 124 with a maximum 125 remaining to be won and that reducing to 100 after Mexico.
"The main headline is that for me (it is) the best race he's delivered so far," said Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff.
"The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional".
McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris finished fifth on a one stop strategy after being passed by both Verstappen and Leclerc on lap 47 of 56 with his tyres struggling. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, and ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri.
Liam Lawson was ninth for Racing Bulls and Pierre Gasly took the final point for Alpine.
Antonelli made a flying getaway and was 2.3 seconds clear at the end of the opening lap while the Ferrari pair took the fight to slow-starting Verstappen for second place.
Leclerc went ahead, before being passed again by the Red Bull, and nearly made contact with Hamilton after the uphill scramble off the grid.
The virtual safety car was briefly deployed on lap two to allow marshals to clear debris and Russell, who had started sixth, had to serve a five second penalty at his sole stop after stewards ruled he had gained an advantage on Piastri on the opening lap at Turn 13.
Russell was then unable to find a way past the McLaren.
"Six good laps, 50 bad laps," he said of his race. "I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint. The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that's the least of my worries after such a bad weekend.
"For me, as long as we're in the constructors' (lead), that's the main thing. Obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest, but P2, P3, P5 is not champion, so it doesn't mean anything."
Haas's Ollie Bearman also collected a 10 second penalty for causing a collision with Gasly and retired at the half-distance.

BRASILIA: Brazil's Supreme Court extended voting in the country's presidential election by two hours on Sunday (Oct 25), leading the electoral authority to pause a vote count that had already started publishing early-stage results.
The election pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro.
Polls were initially set to close at 5pm Brasilia time (4am Monday, Singapore time) and will now close at 7pm after Supreme Justice Cristiano Zanin accepted a request by Lula's campaign to extend voting, pointing to public transportation issues in three cities in the state of Bahia.
Zanin's decision landed right around the 5pm cutoff, when the electoral court had already started publishing results that showed Lula leading Bolsonaro with 0.25 per cent of ballot counted. Lula had 57.66 per cent of votes, compared with 42.34 per cent for Bolsonaro, the early count showed.

PAUSE ADDS UNCERTAINTY The pause over the vote count injects uncertainty into a Brazilian electoral process still grappling with the fallout from 2022, when Jair Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat to Lula. His supporters later invaded government buildings in protests against the result, and Bolsonaro received a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup.
Lula had asked electoral authorities to extend voting in at least nine states after his campaign alleged some officials reduced election day public transportation, impacting voters' ability to get to the polls.
Earlier on Sunday, a court in Bahia, a Lula stronghold in the Northeast, ordered the arrest of a top transportation official in the city of Salvador over allegations that he directed a reduction in the city’s bus fleet.
Bolsonaro had also asked for voting to be extended in at least three states, citing bad weather.

items.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) detected three People's Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft sorties, six PLA Navy (PLAN) vessels, and nine official ships operating around the country up until 6 ...
items.body:
Taiwan detects 3 Chinese aircraft, 6 naval vessels, 9 official ships around its territory: MND Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) detected three People's Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft sorties, six PLA Navy (PLAN) vessels, and nine official ships operating around the country up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) on Monday.
ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 09:59 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 09:59 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) detected three People's Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft sorties, six PLA Navy (PLAN) vessels, and nine official ships operating around the country up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) on Monday. In a statement on X post, it stated, “3 sorties of PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships operating around Taiwan detected up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today.”
According to the ministry, one of the three aircraft sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwan's southwestern and eastern Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ). The Republic of China (ROC) Armed Forces monitored the situation and responded. “1 out of 3 sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwan’s southwestern and eastern part ADIZ. #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded,” the ministry added.
Earlier on Thursday, Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense (MND) stated that it detected three Chinese naval vessels and seven official ships operating in the waters surrounding Taiwan up until 6 am (local time). According to the ministry, the Republic of China (ROC) Armed Forces maintained close surveillance of the maritime activities and deployed appropriate assets to respond to the situation.
In a statement posted on social media platform X, Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense said: "3 PLAN vessels and 7 official ships operating around #Taiwan detected up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today. #ROCArmed Forces have monitored the situation and responded." The ministry further stated that no Chinese military aircraft were detected operating in the vicinity of Taiwan during the designated 24-hour tracking window.
"No flight path illustration is provided, as we did not detect #PLA aircraft operating around Taiwan during this timeframe," the ministry added. Meanwhile, more than half of Taiwanese respondents believe the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is responsible for undermining peace across the Taiwan Strait, reflecting growing public concern over Beijing’s activities and pressure on Taiwan, according to a survey released by Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council (MAC), as reported by The Taipei Times.
According to The Taipei Times, 52.3 per cent of respondents blamed the CCP for destabilising cross-strait relations, rising from 47.4 per cent in a similar poll conducted in May. The findings indicate an increase of nearly five percentage points in public attribution of responsibility to Beijing. Meanwhile, 28.5 per cent believed both Taiwan and China shared responsibility, down from 33.3 per cent in May. Only 6 per cent held Taiwan solely responsible, compared with 7.9 per cent previously. Another 13.2 per cent expressed no opinion or said they were unsure, up from 11.3 per cent. (ANI)

items.summary: Victory makes the Workers' Party member extend his record as the second longest-serving holder of the office, behind Getúlio Vargas ...
items.body:
80-year old Left leader Lula da Silva elected Brazil President for fourth time Victory makes the Workers' Party member extend his record as the second longest-serving holder of the office, behind Getúlio Vargas
ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 09:59 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 09:59 IST

Brazil President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Left leader, 80-year-old former factory worker and current Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won re-election on Sunday, has he defeated Flávio Bolsonaro, in a heated run-off after being tied during the first round of elections. According to Brazilian Media and projections by Datafolha a, with 99.77% of the votes counted, the incumbent president had 51.76% of the valid votes in the second round of the election, compared to 48.24% for Bolsonaro junior.
Victory makes the Workers' Party member extend his record as the second longest-serving holder of the office, behind Getúlio Vargas. By the end of his last term, he will have been in power for 16 years, a record in Brazil's democratic history. The victory follows a campaign dominated by concerns over the cost of living, crime and corruption. CNN reported that it is also the first time since the return of direct presidential elections in 1989 that a candidate has won the presidency after finishing second in the first round.
Lula, who first governed Brazil between 2003 and 2010, has faced a tough reelection battle because of concerns about the cost of living and security. Bolsonaro made a tough-on-crime approach the cornerstone of his campaign and pledged to bring down food costs. Both Presidential candidates had been hit by corruption allegations involving family members and allies. Lula had spent more than a year in prison on corruption convictions that were eventually annulled.
The results of Sunday's run-off came after a heated election day, with voting being extended by two hours following last-minute pleas from both candidates to electoral authorities. According to CNN, Lula's victory will have repercussions beyond Brazil, keeping Latin America’s largest country on a more independent foreign-policy path under Lula, who has emphasized Brazil’s sovereignty and closer ties with the Global South and China amid tensions with the Trump administration.
Lula began his political career in the 1970s as a union leader. He then helped found the Workers' Party, which he represented as a presidential candidate three times until he finally won it in 2002. He was re-elected four years later and was succeeded by one of his cabinet ministers, Dilma Rousseff, in 2010. She was re-elected in 2014. (ANI)

KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes , critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been fully restored after recent issues.
Speaking to Ukraine's TSN television channel, he said SpaceX's Starshield satellite internet had been working at speeds of up to 420kmh since early on Saturday (Oct 24) morning, after it had been throttled earlier in October amid diplomatic pressure on Kyiv from Washington.
Zelenskyy said he discussed both issues in a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, casting the changes as results of that meeting.
Speaking about the upcoming technical talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in November, Zelenskyy said Ukraine would not discuss limits to its armed forces, or enforced post-war neutrality. Kyiv has long sought entry into the NATO alliance despite the reticence of some members.
Zelenskyy also renewed his push for a trilateral US-brokered meeting between him and Vladimir Putin.
The Ukrainian leader has long argued Putin is the only person in Russia who can make major decisions to end the war or meaningfully discuss core issues, such as the fate of the nearly 20 per cent of Ukraine that Russia occupies.
"The issue of territories is a red line that can be discussed exclusively at the level of leaders," Zelenskyy said.

JERUSALEM: Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday (Oct 25) said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country's reputation.
The public intervention by the prominent hedge fund manager, who is Jewish, comes just two days before Israel's general election, in which polls show a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition.
Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, "Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions."

"This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large," he said.
The Abraham Accords are the 2020 agreement, mediated by President Donald Trump's first administration, that saw Israel establish relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. It later reestablished official ties with Morocco.
Representatives for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Related:

Thousands rally in Tel Aviv against Netanyahu ahead of vote

Middle East conflict: Israel faces pressure from Western allies over Gaza and West Bank

As ministers in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel's minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank.
Several countries, including Britain, Canada and Australia, have imposed sanctions on the two ministers over accusations that they have incited violence against Palestinians in the West Bank.
Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 parliamentary seats at Tuesday's election, up from 6, while Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8, up from 7.
Ackman, who was visiting Israel last week, and who along with his wife Neri Oxman owns 5 percent of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, supported Donald Trump's candidacy for president in 2024. Trump last week publicly endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister.
Nimrod Goren, the president of Israeli think tank Mitvim, said Ackman's statement appeared to reflect a desire among Trump's circles for Netanyahu to drop his far-right allies after the vote to form a 'unity government' with opposition parties.
However, Gadi Eisenkot, the leading challenger to Netanyahu, and other opposition party leaders have ruled out forming a government with Israel's longest-serving prime minister.
Speaking at a Tel Aviv conference on Thursday, Ackman praised Netanyahu, who he said had done a good job in protecting and defending Israel since the Oct 7 2023 Hamas attack.
Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday calling for an independent inquiry into the attack that killed around 1,200 people.

items.body:
Home / World News / Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout

Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 8:42 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity.
  Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses.
  It was not immediately clear from Musk's post what he meant by the deal being "closed" or whether investors had agreed to pricing for the debt.
  "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter," Musk said in the post.  
 

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen.
Also Read

Musk's donations top $445 million in push for Republicans in US midterms

Trump admin offers mixed messages on limits to Ukraine's Starshield access

  Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of Nvidia artificial intelligence chips.
  The funding highlights the enormous capital requirement of the AI boom, as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out the computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.
  Musk said debt markets "have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers."

  As a result, he predicted neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, and later said SpaceX won't buy any neoclouds, calling it "pointless."
  Unlike larger cloud firms that serve a broad range of industries, neoclouds such as Nebius and CoreWeave mostly focus on tech customers and offer capacity tailored for AI technology.
  Investors have started betting against US neocloud and data center companies, after fears that their debt-fueled AI buildout was becoming unsustainable sparked a selloff. 
AI investment, chip manufacturing   SpaceX's revenue climbed 161% from a year ago to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX's heavy investment in AI was paying off.

  The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink satellite internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service.
  Terafab, the chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla in Austin, should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year as it aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028.
  Musk told investors in a conference call last week that a merger of his two companies would be "a good idea," citing growing overlap between them.
  Prior to its blockbuster IPO, SpaceX listed "manufacturing our own GPUs" among the substantial capital expenditures it is undertaking in its S-1 statement, warning prospective investors of its big spending plans to develop AI and other technologies.  

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

CARACAS/BARQUISIMETO: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned home on Sunday (Oct 25) after nearly a year away, and after several failed attempts to return that strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration.
"I'm here. With you all," the Nobel Peace Prize- winner wrote on X.
She appeared at a church in western Lara state, according to images shared by her press team, and was greeted by bystanders who sang the national anthem and shouted "liberty!" as she left in an SUV, a Reuters witness said. She will travel to Caracas by road, her team said.
Her efforts to return have tested her relationship with the Trump administration , which she has sought to cultivate as an ally since before it removed President Nicolas Maduro from power in January.

LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc.
Building on previous comments about the need to rethink ties with Brussels, Burnham told the Sunday Times that the influx of EU workers into Britain before Brexit had posed very significant challenges. "But, at the same time, it was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he said.
"Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different. The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we’ve just got to have an honest discussion about those things."
Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

In September, two months after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour Party leader and prime minister, Burnham said Britain should consider options for its relationship with the EU, including possibly rejoining the bloc one day.
He had previously backed the pledges of Starmer's government which included no return to freedom of movement which Brussels sets as a condition for being part of the bloc's single market.
In his interview with the Sunday Times, conducted on Oct 19, Burnham said the issue of freedom of movement could be considered as part of a broader reset of Britain's relationship with the EU, including on data sharing and migration.

Related:

Burnham hopes for EU deal next month, stirs Brexit debate

'Welcome back,' says Macron, as UK PM opens door to EU return

"You've got to see it in the round, rather than just looking at freedom of movement on its own," he said.
Burnham, who is trying to find ways to speed up Britain's economy, is due to meet top EU officials for a summit on Nov 20.
He said he could not imagine recommending that Britain adopt the euro currency or the EU's border-free travel arrangements.
A new referendum would be needed to rejoin the EU but not necessarily to join the bloc's single market or a customs union, the Sunday Times quoted Burnham as saying.
Former Conservative finance minister Jeremy Hunt, who campaigned to stay in the EU in 2016, said it would be a mistake to reopen one of the fundamental debates of the referendum and he said relaxing immigration rules would hurt people in Britain.
"I think it will be a hammer blow to getting people off welfare and into work," Hunt told Sky News.

DETROIT: US President Donald Trump will rally Republicans in eastern Michigan on Sunday (Oct 25), a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's midterm elections. 
Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests, an open-seat race between former Republican Representative Mike Rogers and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that will help decide control of the chamber.
Despite repeatedly attacking El-Sayed from the Oval Office and at rallies across the country, the Republican president had not yet campaigned in Michigan this year. 
If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint El-Sayed as a Muslim extremist and repeatedly mocked his middle name, Mohamed, a common Muslim name.

El-Sayed has dismissed the accusation and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "Faith is a thing there’s just too little of in Washington."
Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. 
"If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers said at a debate last week. 
El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group and says it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States.

Related:

Trump's approval rating sinks to record low two weeks before midterm elections

Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms

At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks on El-Sayed as an attempt by opponents to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are". 
The former president compared it to his experience as the target of false claims that he was born in Kenya.
"We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." 
Trump's rally in Port Huron, part of an area of Michigan that he won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66 per cent of the vote, will also highlight the US-Canada tariff standoff. 
The trade fight has affected the Detroit-based US auto industry, prompting Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy. 
Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US Senate and US House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns home after fraught year away
items.author: Vivian Sequera, Sarah Kinosian, Keren Torres
items.creator: Vivian Sequera, Sarah Kinosian, Keren Torres
items.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado was greeted by tens of thousands of cheering supporters as she made her way by car to Caracas on Sunday night, after she arrived home following several failed return attempts which have strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration.
items.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado was greeted by tens of thousands of cheering supporters as she made her way by car to Caracas on Sunday night, after she arrived home following several failed return attempts which have strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration.
"This country is giving lessons to everyone," she shouted as her convoy entered the capital, leaning out of the sunroof to shake hands and hug raucous supporters
Nobel Peace Prize laureate Machado, who was prevented from challenging deposed leader Nicolas Maduro for the presidency in 2024, has been out of the country for 10 months and spent the previous year in hiding following the disputed election.
On Sunday morning, Machado appeared at a church in western Lara state and was greeted by bystanders who sang the national anthem and shouted "liberty!" as she left in an SUV, a Reuters witness said.
She then traveled to the capital in a journey that took eight hours because of crowds. By the time she neared Caracas, festooned in rosaries handed to her by followers, the highway was all but blocked by cheering supporters.
"For the reunion of every family, for freedom of every political prisoner, for the freedom of Venezuela," she wrote on social media.
Machado's return was coordinated with the US, Panamanian and Colombian governments, according to a person briefed directly on her movements, who added Trump approved her return and was kept informed about it.
At the White House on Sunday, Trump said he did not know anything about Machado's return and suggested the US would continue to back Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez.
"She's a very nice woman," he said, referring to Machado. "But we're doing really well in Venezuela.”
The White House and the State Department did not respond to Reuters questions on the matter.
RETURN PREVIOUSLY DELAYED Machado's efforts to return have tested her relationship with the Trump administration, which [USN:L4N3W51LU TEXT:"she sought to cultivate as an ally"] even before it captured Maduro in January and took him to New York for trial.
Trump has repeatedly expressed support for Rodriguez, a former deputy to Maduro, and hailed deals on oil production and other business ventures by US companies in the South American country. Trump said in September it was [USN:L1N44V0SA TEXT:"too soon to consider democratic elections"] in Venezuela.
US officials have asked Machado at least once to [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"delay her return"], Reuters reported in June, and she has made [USN:L1N45F02O TEXT:"several failed attempts"] to enter the country. Her team did not disclose details of how she returned.
Machado traveled in a private plane from Panama to Colombia and crossed overland on Sunday to Venezuela, four people familiar with her trip told Reuters.
One person briefed on her movements said the flight took place late last week and US security contractors guarded her during the journey. Rodriguez and the country's authorities were warned by the US not to interfere or threaten her safety, the person said.
"The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms. Machado to Venezuela are the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks which have already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement on Sunday.
"We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."
A faction of the opposition and the interim government held a round of talks this month, with the aim of remaking the top court and electoral council, among other goals, ahead of eventual elections. The talks have not included Machado's political movement.
The Venezuelan Communications Ministry, which handles all press queries for the government, did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Machado's return.
SUPPORTERS CHEER MACHADO ON ROUTE "Maria Corina Machado will achieve liberty and democracy in Venezuela," said Hernan Adames, 69, as he celebrated with other supporters in Barquisimeto.
Zuleima Granadillo, 61, an employee at the Ministry of Education, waited for Machado at a point on the highway in Aragua state, closer to Caracas.
"What does Machado’s arrival mean? All paths are opening up for us, the future is opening up, we have a light, and we are going all the way to the end," she said.
"This dictatorship is already over with the arrival of our leader."
Machado plans to meet victims of the deadly earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, as well as the families of political prisoners, the international community and various leaders from the democratic movement in Venezuela, David Smolansky, her top foreign affairs adviser, told Reuters.
"She will work proactively for a date for free and fair elections," he added.
International energy firms committed last month to [USN:L1N44U0I0 TEXT:"expanding projects"] in the country in a signing ceremony overseen by Rodriguez and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright.
Machado has said that only a "serious, democratic government" can provide the stability needed by investors.
She had been barred by Maduro's government from exiting Venezuela but she secretly left in late 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, after spending more than a year living mostly in hiding.
Machado's Vente Venezuela movement [USN:L6N4611CS TEXT:"released an app on Saturday"] to collect voter registration information from Venezuelans abroad. The group hopes eventually to share data from the app, which was built by 15 staff over the last 18 months, with a reformed electoral council so users can be officially added to voter rolls.
Edmundo Gonzalez, a former presidential candidate for Machado's movement who has been living in Spain, said on X he would soon join her in Venezuela.
